कृतसादृश्यरूपौ तौ तावेवाभिमुखौ स्थितौ ॥ 25.38 ॥
1.25.m:
The two best of beings assumed forms identical to Viṣṇu and Jiṣṇu;
having assumed similar forms, they stood facing them.

1.25.s:
tatastau procaturddaityau brahmāṇaṃ dāruṇaṃ vacaḥ.
asmākaṃ yudhyamānānāṃ madhye vai prāśniko bhava .. 25.39 ..
1.25.d:
ततस्तौ प्रोचतुर्द्दैत्यौ ब्रह्माणं दारुणं वचः।
अस्माकं युध्यमानानां मध्ये वै प्राश्निको भव ॥ 25.39 ॥
1.25.m:
Then the two daityas spoke cruel words to Brahmā:
“Between us who are fighting, become an umpire!”

1.25.s:
tatastau jalamāviśya saṃstambhyāpaḥ svamāyayā .
cakratustumulaṃ yuddhaṃ yasya yenepsitaṃ tadā .. 25.40 ..
1.25.d:
ततस्तौ जलमाविश्य संस्तम्भ्यापः स्वमायया ।
चक्रतुस्तुमुलं युद्धं यस्य येनेप्सितं तदा ॥ 25.40 ॥
1.25.m:
Then both, entering the water and holding back the waters with their māyā,
fought a tumultuous battle, each with whom he desired at that time.

1.25.s:
teṣāntu yudhyamānānāṃ divyaṃ varṣaśataṅgatam.
na ca yuddhamadotseko hyanyonyaṃ saṃnyavarttata .. 25.41 ..
1.25.d:
तेषान्तु युध्यमानानां दिव्यं वर्षशतङ्गतम्।
न च युद्धमदोत्सेको ह्यन्योन्यं संन्यवर्त्तत ॥ 25.41 ॥
1.25.m:
While they were fighting, a divine hundred years passed,
and their frenzy for battle against each other did not cease.

1.25.s:
lakṣaṇadvayasaṃsthānādrūpavantau sthiteṅgitau.
sādṛśyādvyākulamanā brahmā dhyānamupāgamat .. 25.42 ..
1.25.d:
लक्षणद्वयसंस्थानाद्रूपवन्तौ स्थितेङ्गितौ।
सादृश्याद्व्याकुलमना ब्रह्मा ध्यानमुपागमत् ॥ 25.42 ॥
1.25.m:
They had handsome forms from the presence of two marks, with steady gestures;
confused in mind by their resemblance, Brahmā resorted to meditation.

1.25.s:
sa tayorantaraṃ buddhvā brahmā divyena cakṣuṣā.
padmakesarajaṃ sūkṣmaṃ babandha kavacantayoḥ.
āmekhalañca gātrañca tato mantramudāharat .. 25.43 ..
1.25.d:
स तयोरन्तरं बुद्ध्वा ब्रह्मा दिव्येन चक्षुषा।
पद्मकेसरजं सूक्ष्मं बबन्ध कवचन्तयोः।
आमेखलञ्च गात्रञ्च ततो मन्त्रमुदाहरत् ॥ 25.43 ॥
1.25.m:
Discerning their difference with his divine eye, Brahmā
bound on both of them a fine armor made of lotus filaments
down to the waist and the limbs; then he uttered a mantra.

1.25.s:
japatastvabhavatkanyā viśvarūpasamutthitā.
padmenduvadanaprakhyā padmahastā śubhā satī.
tāṃ dṛṣṭvā vyathitau daityau bhayādvarṇavivarjjitau .. 25.44 ..
1.25.d:
जपतस्त्वभवत्कन्या विश्वरूपसमुत्थिता।
पद्मेन्दुवदनप्रख्या पद्महस्ता शुभा सती।
तां दृष्ट्वा व्यथितौ दैत्यौ भयाद्वर्णविवर्ज्जितौ ॥ 25.44 ॥
1.25.m:
As he chanted, a maiden arose, manifested in all-pervading form,
resplendent with a face like a lotus and the moon, holding a lotus in her hand, auspicious and chaste.
Seeing her, the two daityas were distressed, losing color out of fear.

1.25.s:
tataḥ provāca tāṃ kanyāṃ brahmā madhurayā girā.
kā'tra tvamavagantavyā brūhi satyamanindite .. 25.45 ..
1.25.d:
ततः प्रोवाच तां कन्यां ब्रह्मा मधुरया गिरा।
काऽत्र त्वमवगन्तव्या ब्रूहि सत्यमनिन्दिते ॥ 25.45 ॥
1.25.m:
Then Brahmā spoke to that maiden in a sweet voice:
“Who are you to be known here? Speak the truth, O blameless one!”

1.25.s:
sāmnā saṃpūjya sā kanyā brahmāṇaṃ prāñjalistadā .
mohinīṃ viddhi māṃ māyāṃ viṣṇoḥ sandeśakāriṇīm .. 25.46 ..
1.25.d:
साम्ना संपूज्य सा कन्या ब्रह्माणं प्राञ्जलिस्तदा ।
मोहिनीं विद्धि मां मायां विष्णोः सन्देशकारिणीम् ॥ 25.46 ॥
1.25.m:
Having honored Brahmā with conciliation, that maiden, with folded hands, then [said]:
“Know me to be the enchanting māyā, doing the bidding of Viṣṇu.

1.25.s:
tvayā saṅkīrttyamānā'haṃ brahman prāptā tvarāyutā.
asyāḥ prītamanā brahmā gauṇaṃ nāma cakāra ha .. 25.47 ..
1.25.d:
त्वया सङ्कीर्त्त्यमानाऽहं ब्रह्मन् प्राप्ता त्वरायुता।
अस्याः प्रीतमना ब्रह्मा गौणं नाम चकार ह ॥ 25.47 ॥
1.25.m:
Praised by you, O Brahman, I have arrived with haste.”
Pleased in mind with her, Brahmā indeed gave her secondary names:

1.25.s:
mayā ca vyāhṛtā yasmāttvañcaiva samupasthitā.
mahāvyāhṛtirityeva nāma te vicariṣyati .. 25.48 ..
1.25.d:
मया च व्याहृता यस्मात्त्वञ्चैव समुपस्थिता।
महाव्याहृतिरित्येव नाम ते विचरिष्यति ॥ 25.48 ॥
1.25.m:
“Since you were invoked (*vyāhṛtā*) by me, and you appeared,
your name shall be known as Mahāvyāhṛti.

1.25.s:
utthitā ca śiro bhittvā sāvitrī tena cocyate.
ekānaṃśāttu yasmāttvamanekāṃśā bhaviṣyasi .. 25.49 ..
1.25.d:
उत्थिता च शिरो भित्त्वा सावित्री तेन चोच्यते।
एकानंशात्तु यस्मात्त्वमनेकांशा भविष्यसि ॥ 25.49 ॥
1.25.m:
And since you arose having split the head, you are called Sāvitrī;
since you will become multifaceted from being undivided (*ekānaṃśā*),

1.25.s:
gauṇāni tāvadetāni karmajānyaparāṇi ca.
nāmāni te bhaviṣyanti matprasādāt śubhānane .. 25.50 ..
1.25.d:
गौणानि तावदेतानि कर्मजान्यपराणि च।
नामानि ते भविष्यन्ति मत्प्रसादात् शुभानने ॥ 25.50 ॥
1.25.m:
such are these secondary names, and there will be others born of action,
that will be yours through my grace, O fair-faced one!”

1.25.s:
tatastau pīḍyamānau tu varamenamayācatām.
anāvṛtaṃ nau maraṇaṃ putratvañca bhavettava .. 25.51 ..
1.25.d:
ततस्तौ पीड्यमानौ तु वरमेनमयाचताम्।
अनावृतं नौ मरणं पुत्रत्वञ्च भवेत्तव ॥ 25.51 ॥
1.25.m:
Then those two, being oppressed, asked a boon of him:
“May our death be in an uncovered place, and may there be sonship to you.”

1.25.s:
tathetyuktvā tatastūrṇamanayat yamasādanam.
anayat kaiṭabhaṃ viṣṇurjiṣṇuścāpyanayanmadhum .. 25.52 ..
1.25.d:
तथेत्युक्त्वा ततस्तूर्णमनयत् यमसादनम्।
अनयत् कैटभं विष्णुर्जिष्णुश्चाप्यनयन्मधुम् ॥ 25.52 ॥
1.25.m:
Saying “So be it,” he then swiftly dispatched [them] to the abode of Yama;
Viṣṇu dispatched Kaiṭabha, and Jiṣṇu dispatched Madhu.

1.25.s:
evantau nihatau daityau viṣṇunā jiṣṇunā saha.
prītena brahmaṇā cātha lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā .. 25.53 ..
1.25.d:
एवन्तौ निहतौ दैत्यौ विष्णुना जिष्णुना सह।
प्रीतेन ब्रह्मणा चाथ लोकानां हितकाम्यया ॥ 25.53 ॥
1.25.m:
In this way the two daityas were slain by Viṣṇu along with Jiṣṇu,
and then by the pleased Brahmā, desiring the welfare of the worlds.

1.25.s:
putratvamīśena yathā hyātmā datto nibodhata.
viṣṇunā jiṣṇunā sārddhaṃ madhukaiṭabhayostathā.
samparāye vyatikrānte brahmā viṣṇumabhāṣata .. 25.54 ..
1.25.d:
पुत्रत्वमीशेन यथा ह्यात्मा दत्तो निबोधत।
विष्णुना जिष्णुना सार्द्धं मधुकैटभयोस्तथा।
सम्पराये व्यतिक्रान्ते ब्रह्मा विष्णुमभाषत ॥ 25.54 ॥

1.25.s:
adya varṣaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ samayaḥ pratyupasthitaḥ.
saṃkṣepasaṃplavaṅghoraṃ svasthānaṃ yāmi cāpyaham .. 25.55 ..
1.25.d:
अद्य वर्षशतं पूर्णं समयः प्रत्युपस्थितः।
संक्षेपसंप्लवङ्घोरं स्वस्थानं यामि चाप्यहम् ॥ 25.55 ॥
1.25.m:
“Today a hundred years are complete, the appointed time has arrived,
the terrible dissolution of cosmic deluge; and I shall go to my own abode.”

1.25.s:
sa tasya vacasā devaḥ saṃhāramakarottadā.
mahīṃ nisthāvarāṃ kṛtvā prakṛtisthāṃśca jaṅgamān .. 25.56 ..
1.25.d:
स तस्य वचसा देवः संहारमकरोत्तदा।
महीं निस्थावरां कृत्वा प्रकृतिस्थांश्च जङ्गमान् ॥ 25.56 ॥
1.25.m:
By his word, the god then brought about dissolution,
rendering the earth devoid of stationary beings, and moving beings dissolved into primal matter.

1.25.s:
yadi govinda bhadrante kṣiptaste yādasāṃ patiḥ.
brūhi yat karaṇīyaṃ syānmayā te lakṣmivarddhana .. 25.57 ..
1.25.d:
यदि गोविन्द भद्रन्ते क्षिप्तस्ते यादसां पतिः।
ब्रूहि यत् करणीयं स्यान्मया ते लक्ष्मिवर्द्धन ॥ 25.57 ॥
1.25.m:
“If, O Govinda, blessings be upon you, the lord of aquatic creatures is cast away by you,
speak what is to be done by me for you, O increaser of Lakṣmī’s fortune?”

1.25.s:
bāḍhaṃ śrṛṇu hemābha padmayone vaco mama .
prasādo yastvayā labdha īśvarāt putralipsayā .. 25.58 ..
1.25.d:
बाढं श्रृणु हेमाभ पद्मयोने वचो मम ।
प्रसादो यस्त्वया लब्ध ईश्वरात् पुत्रलिप्सया ॥ 25.58 ॥
1.25.m:
“Very well, listen, O golden-hued one, born of the lotus, to my word,
to the favor which was attained by you from Īśvara through the desire for a son.”

1.25.s:
tantathā saphalaṃ kṛtvā matto'bhūdanṛṇo bhavān.
caturvidhāni bhūtāni sṛja tvaṃ visṛjasva vā .. 25.59 ..
1.25.d:
तन्तथा सफलं कृत्वा मत्तोऽभूदनृणो भवान्।
चतुर्विधानि भूतानि सृज त्वं विसृजस्व वा ॥ 25.59 ॥
1.25.m: Having made that [boon] fruitful in that way, you have become free of debt to me. / Create the four kinds of beings, or release them [into creation].

1.25.s:
avāpya saṃjñāṅgovindāt padmayoniḥ pitāmahaḥ.
prajāḥ sraṣṭumanāstepe tapa ugraṃ tato mahat .. 25.60 ..
1.25.d:
अवाप्य संज्ञाङ्गोविन्दात् पद्मयोनिः पितामहः।
प्रजाः स्रष्टुमनास्तेपे तप उग्रं ततो महत् ॥ 25.60 ॥
1.25.m: Having received instruction from Govinda, the lotus-born grandfather, / intent on creating creatures, then performed severe and great asceticism.

1.25.s:
tasyaivantapyamānasya na kiñcitsamavarttata.
tato dīrgheṇa kālena duḥkhāt krodho vyavarddhata .. 25.61 ..
1.25.d:
तस्यैवन्तप्यमानस्य न किञ्चित्समवर्त्तत।
ततो दीर्घेण कालेन दुःखात् क्रोधो व्यवर्द्धत ॥ 25.61 ॥
1.25.m: Even as he was thus performing asceticism, nothing whatsoever came to be. / Then, through long passage of time, wrath arose out of distress.

1.25.s:
sakrodhāviṣṭanetrabhyāmapatannaśrubindavaḥ .
tatastebhyo'śrubindubhyo vātapittakaphātmakāḥ .. 25.62 ..
1.25.d:
सक्रोधाविष्टनेत्रभ्यामपतन्नश्रुबिन्दवः ।
ततस्तेभ्योऽश्रुबिन्दुभ्यो वातपित्तकफात्मकाः ॥ 25.62 ॥
1.25.m: Tears fell from his eyes that were overcome with wrath. / Then, from those tear-drops, having the nature of wind, bile, and phlegm,

1.25.s:
mahābhāgā mahāsattvāḥ svastikairabhyalaṅkṛtāḥ.
prakīrṇakeśāḥ sarpāste prādurbhūtā mahāviṣāḥ .. 25.63 ..
1.25.d:
महाभागा महासत्त्वाः स्वस्तिकैरभ्यलङ्कृताः।
प्रकीर्णकेशाः सर्पास्ते प्रादुर्भूता महाविषाः ॥ 25.63 ॥
1.25.m: the serpents were produced—greatly fortunate, endowed with great vitality, adorned with svastikas, / with disheveled hair, and possessing virulent poison.

1.25.s:
sarpāṃstathāgrajān dṛṣṭvā brahmātmānamanindata.
aho dhik tapasā mahyaṃ phalamīdṛśakaṃ yadi.
lokavaināśikī jajñe ādāveva prajā mama .. 25.64 ..
1.25.d:
सर्पांस्तथाग्रजान् दृष्ट्वा ब्रह्मात्मानमनिन्दत।
अहो धिक् तपसा मह्यं फलमीदृशकं यदि।
लोकवैनाशिकी जज्ञे आदावेव प्रजा मम ॥ 25.64 ॥
1.25.m: Seeing the serpents thus as the firstborn, Brahmā reproached himself: / 'Alas, fie! If such is the fruit of my asceticism, / that at the very beginning of my creation destructive offspring have been born to the world!'

1.25.s:
tasya tīvrābhavanmūrcchā krodhāmarṣasamudbhavā.
mūrcchābhitāpena tadā jahau prāṇān prajāpatiḥ .. 25.65 ..
1.25.d:
तस्य तीव्राभवन्मूर्च्छा क्रोधामर्षसमुद्भवा।
मूर्च्छाभितापेन तदा जहौ प्राणान् प्रजापतिः ॥ 25.65 ॥
1.25.m: A severe fainting-fit overcame him, born of anger and indignation. / Under the burning agony of that swoon, Prajāpati then gave up his life-breaths.

1.25.s:
tasyāpratimavīryasya dehāt kāruṇyapūrvakam.
ātmaikādaśa te rudrāḥ prodbhūtā rudatastathā.
rodanāt khalu rudrāste rudratvaṃ tena teṣu tat .. 25.66 ..
1.25.d:
तस्याप्रतिमवीर्यस्य देहात् कारुण्यपूर्वकम्।
आत्मैकादश ते रुद्राः प्रोद्भूता रुदतस्तथा।
रोदनात् खलु रुद्रास्ते रुद्रत्वं तेन तेषु तत् ॥ 25.66 ॥
1.25.m: From the body of that one of matchless vigor, preceded by compassion, / those eleven Rudras arose, crying out in that manner. / Truly, because of their crying (rodana) they are Rudras; by that [act] Rudra-hood belongs to them.

1.25.s:
ye rudrāḥ khalu te prāṇā ye prāṇāste tadātmakāḥ.
prāṇāḥ prāṇabhṛtāṃ jñeyāḥ sarvabhūteṣvavasthitāḥ .. 25.67 ..
1.25.d:
ये रुद्राः खलु ते प्राणा ये प्राणास्ते तदात्मकाः।
प्राणाः प्राणभृतां ज्ञेयाः सर्वभूतेष्ववस्थिताः ॥ 25.67 ॥
1.25.m: Those who are the Rudras are indeed the life-breaths; those that are the life-breaths have their nature. / The life-breaths of breathing creatures are to be known as residing in all beings.

1.25.s:
atyugrasya mahattvasya sādhunā caritasya ca.
tasya prāṇān dadau bhūyastriśūlī nīlalohitaḥ.
lalāṭāt padmayonestu prabhurekādaśātmakaḥ .. 25.68 ..
1.25.d:
अत्युग्रस्य महत्त्वस्य साधुना चरितस्य च।
तस्य प्राणान् ददौ भूयस्त्रिशूली नीललोहितः।
ललाटात् पद्मयोनेस्तु प्रभुरेकादशात्मकः ॥ 25.68 ॥
1.25.m: To him who was exceedingly fierce, of great majesty, and whose conduct was virtuous, / the trident-bearer, Nīlalohita, gave life-breaths again— / the lord consisting of eleven forms [emerging] from the forehead of the lotus-born.

1.25.s:
brahmaṇaḥ so'dadāt prāṇānātmajaḥ sa tadā prabhuḥ.
prahṛṣṭavadano rudraḥ kiṃcit pratyāgatāsavam.
abhyabhāṣattadā devo brahmāṇaṃ paramaṃ vacaḥ .. 25.69 ..
1.25.d:
ब्रह्मणः सोऽददात् प्राणानात्मजः स तदा प्रभुः।
प्रहृष्टवदनो रुद्रः किंचित् प्रत्यागतासवम्।
अभ्यभाषत्तदा देवो ब्रह्माणं परमं वचः ॥ 25.69 ॥
1.25.m: The lord, his son, then gave life-breaths to Brahmā. / With a cheerful face, the god Rudra then addressed supreme words / to Brahmā, whose life-breaths had somewhat returned:

1.25.s:
upayācasva māṃ brahman smarttumarhasi cātmanaḥ.
māṃ ca vetthātmajaṃ rudraṃ prasādaṃ kuru me prabho .. 25.70 ..
1.25.d:
उपयाचस्व मां ब्रह्मन् स्मर्त्तुमर्हसि चात्मनः।
मां च वेत्थात्मजं रुद्रं प्रसादं कुरु मे प्रभो ॥ 25.70 ॥
1.25.m: 'Pray to me, O Brahman; you ought to remember yourself, / and know me as Rudra, your son. Bestow your favor upon me, O lord.'

1.25.s:
śrutvā tvidaṃ vacastasya prabhūtañca manogatam.
pitāmahaḥ prasannātmā netre phullāmbujaprabhaiḥ .. 25.71 ..
1.25.d:
श्रुत्वा त्विदं वचस्तस्य प्रभूतञ्च मनोगतम्।
पितामहः प्रसन्नात्मा नेत्रे फुल्लाम्बुजप्रभैः ॥ 25.71 ॥
1.25.m: Having heard these abundant words of his, and [knowing] his intention, / the grandfather, serene in mind, [opened] his eyes that shone like blooming lotuses.

1.25.s:
tataḥ pratyāgataprāṇaḥ snigdhagambhīrayā girā.
uvāca bhagavān brahmā śuddhajāmbūnadaprabhaḥ .. 25.72 ..
1.25.d:
ततः प्रत्यागतप्राणः स्निग्धगम्भीरया गिरा।
उवाच भगवान् ब्रह्मा शुद्धजाम्बूनदप्रभः ॥ 25.72 ॥
1.25.m: Then, having his life-breaths restored, the lord Brahmā, / shining like pure gold from the Jambu river, spoke with an affectionate and deep voice:

1.25.s:
bho bho vada mahābhāga ānandayasi me manaḥ.
ko bhavān viśvabhūtistvaṃ sthita ekādaśātmakaḥ .. 25.73 ..
1.25.d:
भो भो वद महाभाग आनन्दयसि मे मनः।
को भवान् विश्वभूतिस्त्वं स्थित एकादशात्मकः ॥ 25.73 ॥
1.25.m: 'O noble one, speak! You gladden my mind. / Who are you, the manifestation of the universe, standing in eleven forms?'

1.25.s:
evamukto bhagavatā brahmaṇā'nantatejasā.
tataḥ pratyavadadrudro hyabhivādyātmajaiḥ saha .. 25.74 ..
1.25.d:
एवमुक्तो भगवता ब्रह्मणाऽनन्ततेजसा।
ततः प्रत्यवदद्रुद्रो ह्यभिवाद्यात्मजैः सह ॥ 25.74 ॥
1.25.m: Thus addressed by the lord Brahmā of infinite splendor, / Rudra, having bowed along with his sons, then replied:

1.25.s:
yatte varamahaṃ brahman yācito viṣṇunā saha.
putro me bhava deveti tvattulyo vāpi dhūrvahaḥ .. 25.75 ..
1.25.d:
यत्ते वरमहं ब्रह्मन् याचितो विष्णुना सह।
पुत्रो मे भव देवेति त्वत्तुल्यो वापि धूर्वहः ॥ 25.75 ॥
1.25.m: 'As to the boon, O Brahman, which I, together with Viṣṇu, was asked by you— / "O god, become my son, or one equal to you, bearing the burden"—

1.25.s:
lokeṣu viśrutaiḥ kāryaṃ sarvairviśvātmasambhavaiḥ.
viṣādantyaja deveśa lokāṃstvaṃ sraṣṭumarhasi .. 25.76 ..
1.25.d:
लोकेषु विश्रुतैः कार्यं सर्वैर्विश्वात्मसम्भवैः।
विषादन्त्यज देवेश लोकांस्त्वं स्रष्टुमर्हसि ॥ 25.76 ॥
1.25.m: [that] is to be accomplished by all of us who are renowned in the worlds, born of the soul of the universe. / Cast off despair, O lord of gods; you ought to create the worlds.'

1.25.s:
evaṃ sa bhagavānukto brahmā prītamanābhavat .
rudraṃ pratyavadadbhūyo lokānte nīlalohitam .. 25.77 ..
1.25.d:
एवं स भगवानुक्तो ब्रह्मा प्रीतमनाभवत् ।
रुद्रं प्रत्यवदद्भूयो लोकान्ते नीललोहितम् ॥ 25.77 ॥
1.25.m: Having been thus addressed, the lord Brahmā became delighted in mind. / He spoke again to Rudra, Nīlalohita, at the end of the worlds:

1.25.s:
sāhāyyaṃ mama kāryārthaṃ prajāḥ sṛja mayā saha.
bījī tvaṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ tatprapannastathā bhava.
bāḍhamityeva tāṃ vāṇīṃ pratijagrāha śaṅkaraḥ .. 25.78 ..
1.25.d:
साहाय्यं मम कार्यार्थं प्रजाः सृज मया सह।
बीजी त्वं सर्वभूतानां तत्प्रपन्नस्तथा भव।
बाढमित्येव तां वाणीं प्रतिजग्राह शङ्करः ॥ 25.78 ॥
1.25.m: 'Provide assistance for my work: create creatures along with me. / You are the seed-giver of all beings; therefore, become engaged in that.' / Saying 'Very well,' Śaṅkara accepted those words.

1.25.s:
tataḥ sa bhagavān brahmā kṛṣṇājinavibhūṣitaḥ.
mano'gre so'sṛjaddevo bhūtānāṃ dhāraṇāṃ tataḥ.
jihvāṃ sarasvatīñcaiva tatastāṃ viśvarūpiṇīm .. 25.79 ..
1.25.d:
ततः स भगवान् ब्रह्मा कृष्णाजिनविभूषितः।
मनोऽग्रे सोऽसृजद्देवो भूतानां धारणां ततः।
जिह्वां सरस्वतीञ्चैव ततस्तां विश्वरूपिणीम् ॥ 25.79 ॥
1.25.m: Then the lord god Brahmā, adorned with a black antelope skin, / created the mind at first, and then the support of living beings; / then the tongue, and Sarasvatī, who possesses the universal form.

1.25.s:
bhṛgumaṅgirasaṃ dakṣaṃ pulastyaṃ pulahaṃ kratum.
vasiṣṭhañca mahātejāḥ sasṛje sapta mānasān .. 25.80 ..
1.25.d:
भृगुमङ्गिरसं दक्षं पुलस्त्यं पुलहं क्रतुम्।
वसिष्ठञ्च महातेजाः ससृजे सप्त मानसान् ॥ 25.80 ॥
1.25.m: Endowed with great splendor, he created seven mind-born [sons]: / Bhṛgu, Aṅgiras, Dakṣa, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, / and Vasiṣṭha.

1.25.s:
putrānātmasamānanyān so'sṛjadviśvasambhavān .
teṣāṃ bhūyo'numārgeṇa gāvo vakrādvijajñire .. 25.81 ..
1.25.d:
पुत्रानात्मसमानन्यान् सोऽसृजद्विश्वसम्भवान् ।
तेषां भूयोऽनुमार्गेण गावो वक्राद्विजज्ञिरे ॥ 25.81 ॥
1.25.m: He created other sons equal to himself, from whom the universe arises. / Following after them, cattle were further born from his mouth,

1.25.s:
oṅkārapramukhān vedānabhimānyāśca devatāḥ.
evametān yatāproktān brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ .. 25.82 ..
1.25.d:
ओङ्कारप्रमुखान् वेदानभिमान्याश्च देवताः।
एवमेतान् यताप्रोक्तान् ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ॥ 25.82 ॥
1.25.m: as well as the Vedas headed by the Oṅkāra and the presiding deities. / Thus, to these mind-born sons headed by Dakṣa,

1.25.s:
dakṣādyān mānasān putrān provāca bhagavān prabhuḥ.
prajāḥ sṛjata bhadraṃ vo rudreṇa saha dhīmatā .. 25.83 ..
1.25.d:
दक्षाद्यान् मानसान् पुत्रान् प्रोवाच भगवान् प्रभुः।
प्रजाः सृजत भद्रं वो रुद्रेण सह धीमता ॥ 25.83 ॥
1.25.m: just as described, the lord and sovereign Brahmā, grandfather of the worlds, said: / 'Create creatures, may prosperity be yours, along with the wise Rudra.'

1.25.s:
anugamya mahātmānaṃ prajānāṃ patayastadā.
vayamicchāmahe deva prajāḥ sraṣṭuṃ tvayā saha.
brahmaṇastveṣa sandeśastava caiva maheśvara .. 25.84 ..
1.25.d:
अनुगम्य महात्मानं प्रजानां पतयस्तदा।
वयमिच्छामहे देव प्रजाः स्रष्टुं त्वया सह।
ब्रह्मणस्त्वेष सन्देशस्तव चैव महेश्वर ॥ 25.84 ॥
1.25.m: Approaching the great-souled [Rudra], the lords of creatures then [said]: / 'O god, we wish to create offspring along with you. / For this is the command of Brahmā and of you, O Maheśvara.'

1.25.s:
tairevamukto bhagavān rudraḥ provāca tān prabhuḥ.
brahmaṇaścātmajā mahyaṃ prāṇān gṛhya ca vai surāḥ .. 25.85 ..
1.25.d:
तैरेवमुक्तो भगवान् रुद्रः प्रोवाच तान् प्रभुः।
ब्रह्मणश्चात्मजा मह्यं प्राणान् गृह्य च वै सुराः ॥ 25.85 ॥
1.25.m: Thus addressed by them, the lord Rudra said to them: / 'And you gods, holding the life-breaths of Brahmā and myself,

1.25.s:
kṛtvāgrajāgrajānetān brāhmaṇānātmajānmama.
brahmādistambaparyantān saptalokānmamātmakān.
bhavantaḥ sraṣṭumarhanti vacanānmama svasti vaḥ .. 25.86 ..
1.25.d:
कृत्वाग्रजाग्रजानेतान् ब्राह्मणानात्मजान्मम।
ब्रह्मादिस्तम्बपर्यन्तान् सप्तलोकान्ममात्मकान्।
भवन्तः स्रष्टुमर्हन्ति वचनान्मम स्वस्ति वः ॥ 25.86 ॥
1.25.m: having made these Brahmins, the firstborn of the firstborn, my sons, / you ought to create the seven worlds of my own nature, from Brahmā down to a clump of grass, / according to my word. May you fare well!'

1.25.s:
tenaivamuktāḥ pratyūcuḥ rudramādyantriśūlinam.
yathājñāpayase deva tathā tadvai bhaviṣyati .. 25.87 ..
1.25.d:
तेनैवमुक्ताः प्रत्यूचुः रुद्रमाद्यन्त्रिशूलिनम्।
यथाज्ञापयसे देव तथा तद्वै भविष्यति ॥ 25.87 ॥
1.25.m: Having been spoken to in this way by him, they replied to Rudra, the primeval trident-bearer: / 'Just as you command, O god, so indeed shall it be.'

1.25.s:
anumānya mahādevaṃ prajānāṃ patayastadā.
ūcurdakṣaṃ mahātmānaṃ bhavān śreṣṭhaḥ prajāpatiḥ.
tvāṃ puraskṛtya bhadrante prajāḥ srakṣyāmahe vayam .. 25.88 ..
1.25.d:
अनुमान्य महादेवं प्रजानां पतयस्तदा।
ऊचुर्दक्षं महात्मानं भवान् श्रेष्ठः प्रजापतिः।
त्वां पुरस्कृत्य भद्रन्ते प्रजाः स्रक्ष्यामहे वयम् ॥ 25.88 ॥
1.25.m: Having gained the consent of Mahādeva, the lords of creatures then / said to the great-souled Dakṣa: 'You are the foremost Prajāpati. / Placing you at our head, may good befall you, we shall create offspring.'

1.25.s:
evamastviti vai dakṣaḥ pratyapadyata bhāṣitam.
taiḥ saha sraṣṭumārebhe prajākāmaḥ prajāpatiḥ.
sargasthite tataḥ sthāṇau brahmā sargamathāsṛjat .. 25.89 ..
1.25.d:
एवमस्त्विति वै दक्षः प्रत्यपद्यत भाषितम्।
तैः सह स्रष्टुमारेभे प्रजाकामः प्रजापतिः।
सर्गस्थिते ततः स्थाणौ ब्रह्मा सर्गमथासृजत् ॥ 25.89 ॥
1.25.m: 'So be it,' said Dakṣa, accepting what had been spoken. / Desiring progeny, the Prajāpati began to create together with them. / Then, when Sthāṇu was established in creation, Brahmā produced the creation.

1.25.s:
athāsya saptame'tīte kalpe vai sambabhūvatuḥ.
ṛbhuḥ sanatkumāraśca tapo lokanivāsinau.
tatau maharṣīnanyān sa mānasānasṛjat prabhuḥ .. 25.90 ..
1.25.d:
अथास्य सप्तमेऽतीते कल्पे वै सम्बभूवतुः।
ऋभुः सनत्कुमारश्च तपो लोकनिवासिनौ।
ततौ महर्षीनन्यान् स मानसानसृजत् प्रभुः ॥ 25.90 ॥
1.25.m: Then, when his seventh aeon had passed, there were indeed born / Ṛbhu and Sanatkumāra, who dwell in the Tapoloka. / Then the lord created other mind-born great seers.

1.25.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte madhukaiṭabhotpattivināśavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo' dhyāyaḥ .. 25 ..
1.25.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते मधुकैटभोत्पत्तिविनाशवर्णनं नाम पञ्चविंशो' ध्यायः ॥ 25 ॥
1.25.m: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, titled 'The Account of the Origin and Destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha,' in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.26.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.26.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.26.m:
The Sūta said:
Ah, the wonderful secrets, O high-minded one, / have been spoken by you in truth for the sake of blessing the world!

1.26.s:
aho vismayanīyāni rahasyāni mahāmate.
tvayoktāni yathātattvaṃ lokānugrahakāraṇāt .. 26.1 ..
1.26.d:
अहो विस्मयनीयानि रहस्यानि महामते।
त्वयोक्तानि यथातत्त्वं लोकानुग्रहकारणात् ॥ 26.1 ॥

1.26.s:
tatra vai saṃśayo mahyamavatā (vā) reṣu śūlinaḥ.
kiṃ kāraṇaṃ mahādevaḥ kaliṃ prāpya sudāruṇam.
hitvā yugāni pūrvāṇi avatāraṃ karoti vai .. 26.2 ..
1.26.d:
तत्र वै संशयो मह्यमवता (वा) रेषु शूलिनः।
किं कारणं महादेवः कलिं प्राप्य सुदारुणम्।
हित्वा युगानि पूर्वाणि अवतारं करोति वै ॥ 26.2 ॥
1.26.m: In that regard, I have a doubt concerning the descents of the trident-bearer: / What is the reason that Mahādeva, reaching the very dreadful Kali [age], / makes a descent, having abandoned the previous yugas?

1.26.s:
asminmanvantare caiva prāpte vaivasvate prabho.
avatāraṃ kathañcakre etadicchāmi veditum .. 26.3 ..
1.26.d:
अस्मिन्मन्वन्तरे चैव प्राप्ते वैवस्वते प्रभो।
अवतारं कथञ्चक्रे एतदिच्छामि वेदितुम् ॥ 26.3 ॥
1.26.m: And how did he make a descent when this Vaivasvata cosmic age of a Manu arrived, O lord? / This I desire to know.

1.26.s:
na te'styaviditaṃ kiñcidiha loke paratra ca.
bhaktānāmupadeśārthaṃ vinayāt pṛcchato mama.
kathayasva mahāprājña yadi śrāvyaṃ mahāmatam .. 26.4 ..
1.26.d:
न तेऽस्त्यविदितं किञ्चिदिह लोके परत्र च।
भक्तानामुपदेशार्थं विनयात् पृच्छतो मम।
कथयस्व महाप्राज्ञ यदि श्राव्यं महामतम् ॥ 26.4 ॥
1.26.m: There is nothing unknown to you in this world or in the next. / As I ask out of humility for the instruction of devotees, / tell me, O greatly wise one, if it is fit to be heard and of great import.'

1.26.s: ..lomaśa uvāca..
1.26.d: ॥लोमश उवाच॥
1.26.m:
Lomaśa said:
Thus asked, the blessed Vāyu, devoted to the welfare of the world, / the greatly splendid Vāyu, revered by the world, spoke this.

1.26.s:
evaṃ pṛṣṭo'tha bhagavān vāyurlokahite rataḥ.
idamāha mahātejā vāyurlokanamaskṛtaḥ .. 26.5 ..
1.26.d:
एवं पृष्टोऽथ भगवान् वायुर्लोकहिते रतः।
इदमाह महातेजा वायुर्लोकनमस्कृतः ॥ 26.5 ॥

1.26.s:
etadghuptatamaṃ loke yanmāntvaṃ paripṛcchasi.
tatsarvaṃ śrṛṇu gādheya ucyamānaṃ yathākramam .. 26.6 ..
1.26.d:
एतद्घुप्ततमं लोके यन्मान्त्वं परिपृच्छसि।
तत्सर्वं श्रृणु गाधेय उच्यमानं यथाक्रमम् ॥ 26.6 ॥
1.26.m: "This is the most secret thing in the world that you ask of me. / Hear all of it, O son of Gādhi, being told in proper order.

1.26.s:
purā hyekārṇave vṛtte divye varṣasahasrake.
sraṣṭukāmaḥ prajā brahmā cintayāmāsa duḥśitaḥ .. 26.7 ..
1.26.d:
पुरा ह्येकार्णवे वृत्ते दिव्ये वर्षसहस्रके।
स्रष्टुकामः प्रजा ब्रह्मा चिन्तयामास दुःशितः ॥ 26.7 ॥
1.26.m: Long ago, when the single ocean had lasted for a divine thousand years, / Brahmā, wishing to create living beings, pondered while distressed.

1.26.s:
tasya cintayamānasya prādurbhūtaḥ kumārakaḥ.
divyagandhaḥ sudhāpekṣī divyāṃ śrutimudīrayan .. 26.8 ..
1.26.d:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य प्रादुर्भूतः कुमारकः।
दिव्यगन्धः सुधापेक्षी दिव्यां श्रुतिमुदीरयन् ॥ 26.8 ॥
1.26.m: As he was pondering, a youth appeared, / of divine fragrance, awaiting nectar, uttering divine revelation,

1.26.s:
aśabdasparśarūpāntāmagandhāṃ rasavarjjitām.
śrutiṃ hyudīrayan devo yāmavindaccaturmmukhaḥ .. 26.9 ..
1.26.d:
अशब्दस्पर्शरूपान्तामगन्धां रसवर्ज्जिताम्।
श्रुतिं ह्युदीरयन् देवो यामविन्दच्चतुर्म्मुखः ॥ 26.9 ॥
1.26.m: devoid of sound, touch, or form, lacking scent and destitute of taste— / uttering divine revelation, the god whom the four-faced [Brahmā] found.

1.26.s:
tatastu dhyānasaṃyuktastapa āsthāya bhairavam.
cintayāmāsa manasā tritayaṃ ko'nvayantviti .. 26.10 ..
1.26.d:
ततस्तु ध्यानसंयुक्तस्तप आस्थाय भैरवम्।
चिन्तयामास मनसा त्रितयं कोऽन्वयन्त्विति ॥ 26.10 ॥
1.26.m: Then, united with meditation, having undertaken terrible austerity, / he pondered in his mind: 'Who may connect this triad?'

1.26.s:
tasya cintayamānasya prādurbhūtaṃ tadakṣaram.
aśabdasparśarūpañca rasagandhavivarjjitam .. 26.11 ..
1.26.d:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य प्रादुर्भूतं तदक्षरम्।
अशब्दस्पर्शरूपञ्च रसगन्धविवर्ज्जितम् ॥ 26.11 ॥
1.26.m: As he was pondering, that imperishable syllable manifested, / devoid of sound, touch, and form, and destitute of taste and scent.

1.26.s:
athottamaṃ sa lokeṣu svamūrttiñcāpi paśyati.
dhyāyanvai sa tadā devamathainaṃ paśyate punaḥ .. 26.12 ..
1.26.d:
अथोत्तमं स लोकेषु स्वमूर्त्तिञ्चापि पश्यति।
ध्यायन्वै स तदा देवमथैनं पश्यते पुनः ॥ 26.12 ॥
1.26.m: Then he saw the highest form in the worlds, and also his own form; / meditating indeed on the god at that time, he then saw him again:

1.26.s:
taṃ śvetamatha raktañca pītaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ tadā punaḥ.
varṇasthaṃ tatra paśyeta na strī na ca napuṃsakam .. 26.13 ..
1.26.d:
तं श्वेतमथ रक्तञ्च पीतं कृष्णं तदा पुनः।
वर्णस्थं तत्र पश्येत न स्त्री न च नपुंसकम् ॥ 26.13 ॥
1.26.m: white, and then red, and then again yellow and black, / abiding in phonemes; there one could see him as neither female nor neuter.

1.26.s:
tatsarvaṃ suciraṃ jñātvā cintayan hi tadakṣaram .
tasya cintayamānasya kaṇṭhāduttiṣṭhate'kṣaraḥ .. 26.14 ..
1.26.d:
तत्सर्वं सुचिरं ज्ञात्वा चिन्तयन् हि तदक्षरम् ।
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य कण्ठादुत्तिष्ठतेऽक्षरः ॥ 26.14 ॥
1.26.m: Having understood all that for a very long time, while pondering that imperishable syllable, / as he was pondering, the imperishable arose from his throat:

1.26.s:
ekamātro mahāghoṣaḥ śvetavarṇaḥ sunirmalaḥ.
sa oṅkāro bhavedvedaḥ akṣaraṃ vai maheśvaraḥ .. 26.15 ..
1.26.d:
एकमात्रो महाघोषः श्वेतवर्णः सुनिर्मलः।
स ओङ्कारो भवेद्वेदः अक्षरं वै महेश्वरः ॥ 26.15 ॥
1.26.m: having one mora, of great sound, white in color, and completely pure. / That oṃkāra became the Veda; the imperishable syllable is indeed Maheśvara.

1.26.s:
tataścintayamānasya tvakṣaraṃ vai svayambhuvaḥ.
prādurbhūtantu raktantu sa devaḥ prathamaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 26.16 ..
1.26.d:
ततश्चिन्तयमानस्य त्वक्षरं वै स्वयम्भुवः।
प्रादुर्भूतन्तु रक्तन्तु स देवः प्रथमः स्मृतः ॥ 26.16 ॥
1.26.m: Then, as Svayambhū was pondering the imperishable syllable, / a red one appeared; he is remembered as the first god.

1.26.s:
ṛgvedaṃ prathamaṃ tasya tvagnimīḻe purohitam.
etāṃ dṛṣṭvā ṛcaṃ brahmā cintayāmāsa vai punaḥ.
tadakṣaraṃ mahātejāḥ kimetaditi lokakṛt .. 26.17 ..
1.26.d:
ऋग्वेदं प्रथमं तस्य त्वग्निमीḻए पुरोहितम्।
एतां दृष्ट्वा ऋचं ब्रह्मा चिन्तयामास वै पुनः।
तदक्षरं महातेजाः किमेतदिति लोककृत् ॥ 26.17 ॥
1.26.m: His was the first Ṛgveda, 'agnim īḻe purohitam'. / Having seen this ṛc, Brahmā, the creator of the world of great radiance, / pondered again: 'What is this imperishable syllable?'

1.26.s:
tasya cintayamānasya tasminnatha maheśvaraḥ .
dvimātramakṣaraṃ jajñe īśitvena dvimātrikam .. 26.18 ..
1.26.d:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य तस्मिन्नथ महेश्वरः ।
द्विमात्रमक्षरं जज्ञे ईशित्वेन द्विमात्रिकम् ॥ 26.18 ॥
1.26.m: As he was pondering, in him then Maheśvara / arose as an imperishable syllable of two morae, through his lordly nature having two morae.

1.26.s:
tataḥ punardvimātraṃ tu cintayāmāsa cākṣaram.
prādurbhūtaṃ ca raktaṃ tacchedane gṛhya sā yajuḥ .. 26.19 ..
1.26.d:
ततः पुनर्द्विमात्रं तु चिन्तयामास चाक्षरम्।
प्रादुर्भूतं च रक्तं तच्छेदने गृह्य सा यजुः ॥ 26.19 ॥
1.26.m: Then he pondered again upon the imperishable syllable of two morae. / And that red one appeared, grasping that yajus for division:

1.26.s:
iṣe tvorjjetvā vāyavastha devo vaḥ savitā punaḥ.
ṛgveda ekamātrastu dvimātrantu yajuḥ smṛtam .. 26.20 ..
1.26.d:
इषे त्वोर्ज्जेत्वा वायवस्थ देवो वः सविता पुनः।
ऋग्वेद एकमात्रस्तु द्विमात्रन्तु यजुः स्मृतम् ॥ 26.20 ॥
1.26.m: 'iṣe tvorje tvā vāyavastha devo vaḥ savitā' again. / The Ṛgveda has one mora, but the Yajus is remembered as having two morae.

1.26.s:
tato vedaṃ dvimātraṃ tu dṛṣṭvā caiva tadakṣaram.
dvimātraṃ cintayan brahma tvakṣaraṃ punarīśvaraḥ .. 26.21 ..
1.26.d:
ततो वेदं द्विमात्रं तु दृष्ट्वा चैव तदक्षरम्।
द्विमात्रं चिन्तयन् ब्रह्म त्वक्षरं पुनरीश्वरः ॥ 26.21 ॥
1.26.m: Then, having seen the Veda of two morae and that imperishable syllable, / the lord Brahmā pondered again upon the imperishable of two morae.

1.26.s:
tasya cintayamānasya coṅkāraḥ sambabhūva ha.
tatastadakṣaraṃ brahmā oṅkāraṃ samacintayat .. 26.22 ..
1.26.d:
तस्य चिन्तयमानस्य चोङ्कारः सम्बभूव ह।
ततस्तदक्षरं ब्रह्मा ओङ्कारं समचिन्तयत् ॥ 26.22 ॥
1.26.m: As he was pondering, the oṃkāra arose. / Then Brahmā pondered upon that imperishable syllable, the oṃkāra.

1.26.s:
athāpaśyattataḥ pītāmṛcaṃ caiva samutthitām.
agna āyāhi vītaye gṛṇāno havyadātaye .. 26.23 ..
1.26.d:
अथापश्यत्ततः पीतामृचं चैव समुत्थिताम्।
अग्न आयाहि वीतये गृणानो हव्यदातये ॥ 26.23 ॥
1.26.m: Then he saw a yellow ṛc that had arisen: / 'agna āyāhi vītaye gṛṇāno havyadātaye'.

1.26.s:
tatastu sa mahātejā dṛṣṭvā vedānupasthitān.
cintayitvā ca bhagavāṃstrisandhyaṃ yatrrirakṣaram.
trivarṇaṃ yat triṣavaṇamoṅkāraṃ brahmasaṃjñitam .. 26.24 ..
1.26.d:
ततस्तु स महातेजा दृष्ट्वा वेदानुपस्थितान्।
चिन्तयित्वा च भगवांस्त्रिसन्ध्यं यत्र्रिरक्षरम्।
त्रिवर्णं यत् त्रिषवणमोङ्कारं ब्रह्मसंज्ञितम् ॥ 26.24 ॥
1.26.m: Then, of great radiance, having seen the Vedas present, / and having meditated, the blessed lord [perceived] that which has three junctions, three syllables, / three colors, three pressings—the oṃkāra, named Brahman,

1.26.s:
tataśvaiva trisaṃyogāt trivarṇaṃ tu tadakṣaram.
lakṣyālakṣyapradṛśyaṃ ca sahitaṃ tridivaṃ trikam .. 26.25 ..
1.26.d:
ततश्वैव त्रिसंयोगात् त्रिवर्णं तु तदक्षरम्।
लक्ष्यालक्ष्यप्रदृश्यं च सहितं त्रिदिवं त्रिकम् ॥ 26.25 ॥
1.26.m: and then, from the threefold conjunction, that imperishable syllable of three colors, / visible as both the perceptible and imperceptible, united with the triad of heaven,

1.26.s:
trimātraṃ tripadaṃ caiva triyogaṃ caiva śāśvatam.
tasmāttadakṣaraṃ brahmā cintayāmāsa vai prabhuḥ .. 26.26 ..
1.26.d:
त्रिमात्रं त्रिपदं चैव त्रियोगं चैव शाश्वतम्।
तस्मात्तदक्षरं ब्रह्मा चिन्तयामास वै प्रभुः ॥ 26.26 ॥
1.26.m:
having three morae, three feet, three yoking methods, and eternal. / Therefore the lord Brahmā pondered upon that imperishable syllable.

Therefore he then saw that imperishable syllable of the self-existent, in the form of Brahman, / as the radiant god with fourteen faces. / Having placed the oṃkāra at the beginning, he is to be known as Svayambhū.

1.26.s:
tasmāttadakṣaraṃ so'tha brahmarūpaṃ svayambhuvaḥ.
caturddaśamukhaṃ devaṃ paśyate dīptatejasam.
tamoṅkāraṃ sa kṛtvādau vijñeyaḥ sa svayambhuvaḥ .. 26.27 ..
1.26.d:
तस्मात्तदक्षरं सोऽथ ब्रह्मरूपं स्वयम्भुवः।
चतुर्द्दशमुखं देवं पश्यते दीप्ततेजसम्।
तमोङ्कारं स कृत्वादौ विज्ञेयः स स्वयम्भुवः ॥ 26.27 ॥

1.26.s:
caturmukhamukhāttasmādajāyanta caturddaśa.
nānāvarṇāḥ svarā divyamādyaṃ tacca tadakṣaram.
tasmāt triṣaṣṭivarṇā vai akāraprabhavāḥ smṛtāḥ .. 26.28 ..
1.26.d:
चतुर्मुखमुखात्तस्मादजायन्त चतुर्द्दश।
नानावर्णाः स्वरा दिव्यमाद्यं तच्च तदक्षरम्।
तस्मात् त्रिषष्टिवर्णा वै अकारप्रभवाः स्मृताः ॥ 26.28 ॥
1.26.m: From that face of the four-faced one arose fourteen / vowels of diverse colors, divine, the primordial, and that imperishable syllable. / From that, sixty-three phonemes are remembered as originating from the letter 'a'.

1.26.s:
tataḥ sādhāraṇārthāya varṇānāntu svayambhuvaḥ.
akārarūpa ādau tu sthitaḥ sa prathamaḥ svaraḥ .. 26.29 ..
1.26.d:
ततः साधारणार्थाय वर्णानान्तु स्वयम्भुवः।
अकाररूप आदौ तु स्थितः स प्रथमः स्वरः ॥ 26.29 ॥
1.26.m: Then, for the common purpose of all phonemes, / that first vowel stood at the beginning in the form of the letter 'a' of Svayambhū.

1.26.s:
tatastebhyaḥ svarebhyastu caturddaśa mahāmukhāḥ.
manavaḥ samprasūyante divyā manvantare svarāḥ .. 26.30 ..
1.26.d:
ततस्तेभ्यः स्वरेभ्यस्तु चतुर्द्दश महामुखाः।
मनवः सम्प्रसूयन्ते दिव्या मन्वन्तरे स्वराः ॥ 26.30 ॥
1.26.m: Then from those vowels, fourteen great-faced / Manus are born, divine vowels in each cosmic age of a Manu.

1.26.s:
caturddaśamukho yaśca akāro brahmasaṃjñitaḥ.
brahmakalpaḥ samākhyātaḥ sarvavarṇaḥ prajāpatiḥ .. 26.31 ..
1.26.d:
चतुर्द्दशमुखो यश्च अकारो ब्रह्मसंज्ञितः।
ब्रह्मकल्पः समाख्यातः सर्ववर्णः प्रजापतिः ॥ 26.31 ॥
1.26.m: And the letter 'a' with fourteen faces, named Brahman, / is proclaimed as the Brahmakalpa, Prajāpati of all phonemes.

1.26.s:
mukhāttu prathamāttasya manuḥ svāyambhuvaḥ smṛtaḥ.
akārastu sa vijñeyaḥ śvetavarṇaḥ svayambhuvaḥ .. 26.32 ..
1.26.d:
मुखात्तु प्रथमात्तस्य मनुः स्वायम्भुवः स्मृतः।
अकारस्तु स विज्ञेयः श्वेतवर्णः स्वयम्भुवः ॥ 26.32 ॥
1.26.m: From his first face is remembered the Manu Svāyambhuva; / he is to be known as the letter 'a', white in color, belonging to Svayambhū.

1.26.s:
dvitīyāttu mukhāttasya ākāro vai mukhaḥ smṛtaḥ.
nāmnā svārociṣo nāma varṇaḥ pāṇḍura ucyate .. 26.33 ..
1.26.d:
द्वितीयात्तु मुखात्तस्य आकारो वै मुखः स्मृतः।
नाम्ना स्वारोचिषो नाम वर्णः पाण्डुर उच्यते ॥ 26.33 ॥
1.26.m: From his second face, the letter 'ā' is remembered as the face; / by name he is called Svārociṣa, and pale is his color said to be.

1.26.s:
tṛtīyāttu mukhāttasya ikāro yajuṣāṃ varaḥ.
yajurmayaḥ sa cādityo yajurvedo yataḥ smṛtaḥ .. 26.34 ..
1.26.d:
तृतीयात्तु मुखात्तस्य इकारो यजुषां वरः।
यजुर्मयः स चादित्यो यजुर्वेदो यतः स्मृतः ॥ 26.34 ॥
1.26.m: From his third face is the letter 'i', best among the yajuses; / it is composed of yajus and is the Sun, from which the Yajurveda is remembered.

1.26.s:
īkāraḥ sa manurjñeyo raktavarṇaḥ pratāpavān.
tataḥ kṣatraṃ pravarttanta tasmādraktastu kṣatriyaḥ .. 26.35 ..
1.26.d:
ईकारः स मनुर्ज्ञेयो रक्तवर्णः प्रतापवान्।
ततः क्षत्रं प्रवर्त्तन्त तस्माद्रक्तस्तु क्षत्रियः ॥ 26.35 ॥
1.26.m: The letter 'ī' is to be known as that Manu, red in color, majestic. / From him the kṣatriya class proceeded; therefore the kṣatriya is red.

1.26.s:
caturthāttu mukhāttasya ukāraḥ svara ucyate.
varṇatastu smṛtastāmraḥ sa manustāmasaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 26.36 ..
1.26.d:
चतुर्थात्तु मुखात्तस्य उकारः स्वर उच्यते।
वर्णतस्तु स्मृतस्ताम्रः स मनुस्तामसः स्मृतः ॥ 26.36 ॥
1.26.m: From his fourth face the vowel 'u' is proclaimed; / in color it is remembered as coppery; that Manu is remembered as Tāmasa.

1.26.s:
pañcamāttu mukhāttasya ūkāro nāma jāyate.
pītako varṇataścaiva manuścāpi cariṣṇavaḥ .. 26.37 ..
1.26.d:
पञ्चमात्तु मुखात्तस्य ऊकारो नाम जायते।
पीतको वर्णतश्चैव मनुश्चापि चरिष्णवः ॥ 26.37 ॥
1.26.m: From his fifth face the letter 'ū' is born by name; / in color it is yellow, and the Manu is Cariṣṇava.

1.26.s:
tataḥ ṣaṣṭhānmukhāttasya oṅkāraḥ kapilaḥ smṛtaḥ.
variṣṭhaśca tataḥ ṣaṣṭho vijayaḥ sa mahātapāḥ .. 26.38 ..
1.26.d:
ततः षष्ठान्मुखात्तस्य ओङ्कारः कपिलः स्मृतः।
वरिष्ठश्च ततः षष्ठो विजयः स महातपाः ॥ 26.38 ॥
1.26.m: Then from his sixth face the oṃkāra is remembered as tawny; / and then the sixth, most excellent, is Vijaya of great austerities.

1.26.s:
saptamāttu mukhāttasya tato vaivasvato manuḥ.
ṛkāraśca svarastatra varṇataḥ kuṣṇa ucyate .. 26.39 ..
1.26.d:
सप्तमात्तु मुखात्तस्य ततो वैवस्वतो मनुः।
ऋकारश्च स्वरस्तत्र वर्णतः कुष्ण उच्यते ॥ 26.39 ॥
1.26.m: From his seventh face then came the Manu Vaivasvata; / and there the vowel is the letter 'ṛ', in color it is said to be black.

1.26.s:
aṣṭamāttu mukhāttasya ṝkāraḥ śyāmavarṇataḥ.
śyāmākṣarasavarṇaśca tataḥ sāvarṇirucyate .. 26.40 ..
1.26.d:
अष्टमात्तु मुखात्तस्य ॠकारः श्यामवर्णतः।
श्यामाक्षरसवर्णश्च ततः सावर्णिरुच्यते ॥ 26.40 ॥
1.26.m: From his eighth face is the letter 'ṝ', dark in color; / having the same color as the dark syllable, he is therefore called Sāvarṇi.

1.26.s:
mukhāttu navamāttasya lṛkāro navamaḥ smṛtaḥ.
dhūmro vai varṇataścāpi dhūmrasva manurucyate .. 26.41 ..
1.26.d:
मुखात्तु नवमात्तस्य लृकारो नवमः स्मृतः।
धूम्रो वै वर्णतश्चापि धूम्रस्व मनुरुच्यते ॥ 26.41 ॥
1.26.m: From his ninth face, the letter 'lṛ' is remembered as the ninth; / in color it is smoke-colored, and the smoke-colored one is said to be the Manu.

1.26.s:
daśamāttu mukhāttasya lṛkāraḥ prabhurucyate.
samaścaiva savarṇaśca babhau sāvarṇiko manuḥ .. 26.42 ..
1.26.d:
दशमात्तु मुखात्तस्य लृकारः प्रभुरुच्यते।
समश्चैव सवर्णश्च बभौ सावर्णिको मनुः ॥ 26.42 ॥
1.26.m: From his tenth face the lord letter 'ḹ' is proclaimed; / equal and having the same color, the Manu Sāvarṇika shone forth.

1.26.s:
mukhādekādaśāttasya ekāro manurucyate.
piśaṅgo varṇataścaiva piśaṅgo varṇa ucyate .. 26.43 ..
1.26.d:
मुखादेकादशात्तस्य एकारो मनुरुच्यते।
पिशङ्गो वर्णतश्चैव पिशङ्गो वर्ण उच्यते ॥ 26.43 ॥
1.26.m: From his eleventh face the letter 'e' is called the Manu; / it is reddish-brown in color, and reddish-brown is the phoneme said to be.

1.26.s:
dvādaśāttu mukhāttasya aikāro nāma ucyate.
piśaṅgo bhasmavarṇābhaḥ piśaṅgo manurucyate .. 26.44 ..
1.26.d:
द्वादशात्तु मुखात्तस्य ऐकारो नाम उच्यते।
पिशङ्गो भस्मवर्णाभः पिशङ्गो मनुरुच्यते ॥ 26.44 ॥
1.26.m: From his twelfth face the letter 'ai' is proclaimed by name; / reddish-brown with the luster of ash-color, the Manu is called reddish-brown.

1.26.s:
trayodaśānmukhāttasya okāro varṇa ucyate.
pañcavarṇasamāyukta okāro varṇa uttamaḥ .. 26.45 ..
1.26.d:
त्रयोदशान्मुखात्तस्य ओकारो वर्ण उच्यते।
पञ्चवर्णसमायुक्त ओकारो वर्ण उत्तमः ॥ 26.45 ॥
1.26.m: From his thirteenth face the letter 'o' is proclaimed as the phoneme; / endowed with five colors, the letter 'o' is the highest phoneme.

1.26.s:
caturddaśamukhāttasya aukāro varṇa ucyate.
karbūro varṇataścaiva manuḥ sāvarṇirucyate .. 26.46 ..
1.26.d:
चतुर्द्दशमुखात्तस्य औकारो वर्ण उच्यते।
कर्बूरो वर्णतश्चैव मनुः सावर्णिरुच्यते ॥ 26.46 ॥
1.26.m: From his fourteenth face the letter 'au' is proclaimed as the phoneme; / in color it is variegated, and the Manu is called Sāvarṇi.

1.26.s:
ityete manavaścaiva svarā varṇāśca kalpataḥ.
vijñeyā hi yathātattvaṃ svarato varṇatastathā .. 26.47 ..
1.26.d:
इत्येते मनवश्चैव स्वरा वर्णाश्च कल्पतः।
विज्ञेया हि यथातत्त्वं स्वरतो वर्णतस्तथा ॥ 26.47 ॥
1.26.m: Thus these Manus, vowels, and colours from the aeon / are to be known according to truth by their vowel and by their colour.

1.26.s:
parasparasavarṇāśca svarā yasmād vṛtā hi vai .
tasmātteṣāṃ savarṇatvādanvayastu prakīrtitaḥ .. 26.48 ..
1.26.d:
परस्परसवर्णाश्च स्वरा यस्माद् वृता हि वै ।
तस्मात्तेषां सवर्णत्वादन्वयस्तु प्रकीर्तितः ॥ 26.48 ॥
1.26.m: And since vowels of the same colour with each other were chosen, / their lineage is therefore proclaimed on account of having the same colour.

1.26.s:
savarṇāḥ sadṛśāścaiva yasmājjātāstu kalpajāḥ.
tasmāt prajānāṃ loke'smin savarṇāḥ sarvasandhayaḥ .. 26.49 ..
1.26.d:
सवर्णाः सदृशाश्चैव यस्माज्जातास्तु कल्पजाः।
तस्मात् प्रजानां लोकेऽस्मिन् सवर्णाः सर्वसन्धयः ॥ 26.49 ॥
1.26.m: Since those born from the aeon are of the same colour and alike, / therefore among the creatures in this world, all junctions are of the same colour.

1.26.s:
bhaviṣyanti yathāśailaṃ varṇāśca nyāyato'rthataḥ.
abhyāsātsandhayaścaiva tasmājjñeyāḥ svarā iti .. 26.50 ..
1.26.d:
भविष्यन्ति यथाशैलं वर्णाश्च न्यायतोऽर्थतः।
अभ्यासात्सन्धयश्चैव तस्माज्ज्ञेयाः स्वरा इति ॥ 26.50 ॥
1.26.m: The colours will arise according to tradition, properly and meaningfully; / and junctions arise from combination; therefore they are to be known as vowels.

1.26.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte svarotpattirnāma ṣaḍ‌viṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 26 ..
1.26.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते स्वरोत्पत्तिर्नाम षड्‌विंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 26 ॥
1.26.m: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, named "The Origin of the Vowels," in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.27.s: ..ṛṣayaḥ ūcuḥ..
1.27.d: ॥ऋषयः ऊचुः॥
1.27.m:
The seers said:
In this aeon, the manifestation of the great soul / Mahādeva Rudra together with ascetic sages has been declared by you.

1.27.s:
asmin kalpe tvayā coktaḥ prādurbhāvo mahātmanaḥ.
mahādevasya rudrasya sādhakairmunibhiḥ saha .. 27.1 ..
1.27.d:
अस्मिन् कल्पे त्वया चोक्तः प्रादुर्भावो महात्मनः।
महादेवस्य रुद्रस्य साधकैर्मुनिभिः सह ॥ 27.1 ॥

1.27.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.27.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.27.m:
The Sūta said:
The origin of the primary creation has been declared by me in brief; / I shall describe his names along with his forms in detail.

1.27.s:
utpattirādisargasya mayā prokta samāsataḥ.
vistareṇāsya vakṣyāmi nāmāni tanubhiḥ saha .. 27.2 ..
1.27.d:
उत्पत्तिरादिसर्गस्य मया प्रोक्त समासतः।
विस्तरेणास्य वक्ष्यामि नामानि तनुभिः सह ॥ 27.2 ॥

1.27.s:
patnīṣu janayāmāsa mahādevaḥ sutān bahūn.
kalpe'ṣṭame vyatīte tu yasmin kalpe tu tacchṛṇu .. 27.3 ..
1.27.d:
पत्नीषु जनयामास महादेवः सुतान् बहून्।
कल्पेऽष्टमे व्यतीते तु यस्मिन् कल्पे तु तच्छृणु ॥ 27.3 ॥
1.27.m: Mahādeva begot many sons upon his wives / when the eighth aeon had passed; hear now in which aeon:

1.27.s:
kalpādau cātmānastulyaṃ sutaṃ pradhyāyataḥ prabhoḥ.
prādurāsīttatoṅke'sya kumāro nīlalohitaḥ.
taṃ dadhe susvaraṃ ghoraṃ nirdahanniva tejasā .. 27.4 ..
1.27.d:
कल्पादौ चात्मानस्तुल्यं सुतं प्रध्यायतः प्रभोः।
प्रादुरासीत्ततोङ्केऽस्य कुमारो नीललोहितः।
तं दधे सुस्वरं घोरं निर्दहन्निव तेजसा ॥ 27.4 ॥
1.27.m: At the beginning of an aeon, as the lord was meditating upon a son equal to himself, / a blue-and-red boy then appeared in his lap. / He produced a loud, dreadful [cry], as if burning [everything] with his brilliance.

1.27.s:
dṛṣṭvā rudantaṃ sahasā kumāraṃ nīlalohitam.
vka rodiṣi kumāreti brahmā taṃ pratyabhāṣata .. 27.5 ..
1.27.d:
दृष्ट्वा रुदन्तं सहसा कुमारं नीललोहितम्।
व्क रोदिषि कुमारेति ब्रह्मा तं प्रत्यभाषत ॥ 27.5 ॥
1.27.m: Seeing the blue-and-red boy weeping suddenly, / Brahmā spoke to him: 'Boy, why do you weep?'

1.27.s:
so'bravīddehi me nāma prathamaṃ vai pitāmaha.
rudrastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ .. 27.6 ..
1.27.d:
सोऽब्रवीद्देहि मे नाम प्रथमं वै पितामह।
रुद्रस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि इत्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः ॥ 27.6 ॥
1.27.m: He said: 'O Grandfather, give me a first name!' / 'You are Rudra by name, O god,' he was told, and he wept again.

1.27.s:
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt .
nāma dehi dvitīyaṃ me ityuvāca svayambhuvam .. 27.7 ..
1.27.d:
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा रुदन्तं पुनरब्रवीत् ।
नाम देहि द्वितीयं मे इत्युवाच स्वयम्भुवम् ॥ 27.7 ॥
1.27.m: Brahmā said again to him as he wept: 'Why do you weep?' / 'Give me a second name,' he said to Svayambhū.

1.27.s:
bhavastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ṅtyuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ.
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā pratyuvācātha śaṅkaram .. 27.8 ..
1.27.d:
भवस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि ङ्त्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः।
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा प्रत्युवाचाथ शङ्करम् ॥ 27.8 ॥
1.27.m: 'You are Bhava by name, O god,' he was told, and he wept again. / Then Brahmā replied to Śaṅkara: 'Why do you weep?'

1.27.s:
tṛtīyaṃ dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca tam.
śivastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca tam.
śivastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ .. 27.9 ..
1.27.d:
तृतीयं देहि मे नाम इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाच तम्।
शिवस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाच तम्।
शिवस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि इत्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः ॥ 27.9 ॥
1.27.m: 'Give me a third name,' he replied when spoken to. / 'You are Śiva by name, O god,' he replied when spoken to. / 'You are Śiva by name, O god,' he was told, and he wept again.

1.27.s:
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt.
caturthaṃ dehi me nāma ityuvāca svayambhuvam .. 27.10 ..
1.27.d:
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा रुदन्तं पुनरब्रवीत्।
चतुर्थं देहि मे नाम इत्युवाच स्वयम्भुवम् ॥ 27.10 ॥
1.27.m: Brahmā spoke again to him as he wept: 'Why do you weep?' / 'Give me a fourth name,' he said to Svayambhū.

1.27.s:
paśūnāṃ tvaṃ patirdeva ityuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ.
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt .. 27.11 ..
1.27.d:
पशूनां त्वं पतिर्देव इत्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः।
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा रुदन्तं पुनरब्रवीत् ॥ 27.11 ॥
1.27.m: 'You are the lord of beasts (Paśupati), O god,' he was told, and he wept again. / Brahmā spoke again to him as he wept: 'Why do you weep?'

1.27.s:
pañcamaṃ dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca tam.
īśastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ .. 27.12 ..
1.27.d:
पञ्चमं देहि मे नाम इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाच तम्।
ईशस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि इत्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः ॥ 27.12 ॥
1.27.m: 'Give me a fifth name,' he replied when spoken to. / 'You are Īśa by name, O god,' he was told, and he wept again.

1.27.s:
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt.
ṣaṣṭhaṃ me nāma dehīti ityuvācātha taṃ prabhum .. 27.13 ..
1.27.d:
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा रुदन्तं पुनरब्रवीत्।
षष्ठं मे नाम देहीति इत्युवाचाथ तं प्रभुम् ॥ 27.13 ॥
1.27.m: Brahmā spoke again to him as he wept: 'Why do you weep?' / 'Give me a sixth name,' he then said to that lord.

1.27.s:
bhīmastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ .
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt .. 27.14 ..
1.27.d:
भीमस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि इत्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः ।
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा रुदन्तं पुनरब्रवीत् ॥ 27.14 ॥
1.27.m: 'You are Bhīma by name, O god,' he was told, and he wept again. / Brahmā spoke again to him as he wept: 'Why do you weep?'

1.27.s:
saptamaṃ dehi me nāma ityuktaḥ pratyuvāca tam.
ugrastvaṃ deva nāmnāsi ityuktaḥ so'rudatpunaḥ .. 27.15 ..
1.27.d:
सप्तमं देहि मे नाम इत्युक्तः प्रत्युवाच तम्।
उग्रस्त्वं देव नाम्नासि इत्युक्तः सोऽरुदत्पुनः ॥ 27.15 ॥
1.27.m: 'Give me a seventh name,' he replied when spoken to. / 'You are Ugra by name, O god,' he was told, and he wept again.

1.27.s:
kiṃ rodiṣīti taṃ brahmā rudantaṃ punarabravīt.
aṣṭhamaṃ dehi me nāma tvaṃ vibho punarabravīt.
mahādevastu nāmnāsi ityukto virarāma ha .. 27.16 ..
1.27.d:
किं रोदिषीति तं ब्रह्मा रुदन्तं पुनरब्रवीत्।
अष्ठमं देहि मे नाम त्वं विभो पुनरब्रवीत्।
महादेवस्तु नाम्नासि इत्युक्तो विरराम ह ॥ 27.16 ॥
1.27.m: Brahmā spoke again to him as he wept: 'Why do you weep?' / He said again: 'O all-pervading one, give me an eighth name!' / 'You are Mahādeva by name,' he was told, and indeed he ceased.

1.27.s:
labdhvā nāmāni caitāni brahmaṇo nīlalohitaḥ.
provāca nāmnāmeteṣāṃ bhūtāni pradiśeti ha .. 27.17 ..
1.27.d:
लब्ध्वा नामानि चैतानि ब्रह्मणो नीललोहितः।
प्रोवाच नाम्नामेतेषां भूतानि प्रदिशेति ह ॥ 27.17 ॥
1.27.m: Having received these names from Brahmā, the blue-and-red one / said: 'Assign the cosmic forms for these names!'

1.27.s:
tato'bhiśṛṣṭāstanava eṣāṃ nāmnāṃ svayambhuvā.
sūryo mahī jalaṃ vahnirvāyurākāśameva ca .. 27.18 ..
1.27.d:
ततोऽभिशृष्टास्तनव एषां नाम्नां स्वयम्भुवा।
सूर्यो मही जलं वह्निर्वायुराकाशमेव च ॥ 27.18 ॥
1.27.m: Then the bodies corresponding to these names were created by Svayambhū: / the sun, the earth, water, fire, wind, and space;

1.27.s:
dīkṣito brahmaṇaścandra ityete brahmadhātavaḥ.
teṣu pūjyaśca vandyaḥ syādrudrastān hinasti vai .. 27.19 ..
1.27.d:
दीक्षितो ब्रह्मणश्चन्द्र इत्येते ब्रह्मधातवः।
तेषु पूज्यश्च वन्द्यः स्याद्रुद्रस्तान् हिनस्ति वै ॥ 27.19 ॥
1.27.m: the initiated brāhmaṇa, and the moon: these are the fundamental elements of Brahmā. / In these [forms] he is worthy of worship and praise; Rudra harms them [who disrespect them].

1.27.s:
tato'bravīt punarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ nīlalohitam .
dvitīyaṃ nāmadheyante mayā proktaṃ bhaveti yat.
etasyāpo dvitīyā te tanurnāmnā bhaviṣyati .. 27.20 ..
1.27.d:
ततोऽब्रवीत् पुनर्ब्रह्मा तं देवं नीललोहितम् ।
द्वितीयं नामधेयन्ते मया प्रोक्तं भवेति यत्।
एतस्यापो द्वितीया ते तनुर्नाम्ना भविष्यति ॥ 27.20 ॥
1.27.m: Then Brahmā spoke again to that blue-and-red god: / 'As for the second name, Bhava, which was spoken by me for you, / water shall be this second body of yours by name.'

1.27.s:
ityukte yat sthiraṃ tasya śarīrasthaṃ rasātmakam.
tadviveśa tatastoyaṃ tasmādāpo bhavaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.21 ..
1.27.d:
इत्युक्ते यत् स्थिरं तस्य शरीरस्थं रसात्मकम्।
तद्विवेश ततस्तोयं तस्मादापो भवः स्मृतः ॥ 27.21 ॥
1.27.m: When this was said, that which was stable and of the nature of fluid within his body, / into that the water then entered; therefore water is considered to be Bhava.

1.27.s:
yasmādbhavanti bhūtāni tābhyastā bhāvayanti ca.
bhavanādbhāvanāccaiva bhūtānāṃ sambhavaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.22 ..
1.27.d:
यस्माद्भवन्ति भूतानि ताभ्यस्ता भावयन्ति च।
भवनाद्भावनाच्चैव भूतानां सम्भवः स्मृतः ॥ 27.22 ॥
1.27.m: Since beings come to be from them and they bring beings into being, / from coming to be and from bringing into being, the origin of beings is recorded.

1.27.s:
tasmānmūtraṃ purīṣañca nāpsu kurvīta sarvadā.
na snāyedapsu nagnaśca na niṣṭhīvet kadācana .. 27.23 ..
1.27.d:
तस्मान्मूत्रं पुरीषञ्च नाप्सु कुर्वीत सर्वदा।
न स्नायेदप्सु नग्नश्च न निष्ठीवेत् कदाचन ॥ 27.23 ॥
1.27.m: Therefore one should never pass urine or feces in water, / nor should one bathe naked in water, nor ever spit.

1.27.s:
maithunaṃ naiva seveta śiraḥsnānañca varjayet.
na prītaḥ paricakṣīta vahanna saṃsthito'pi vā .. 27.24 ..
1.27.d:
मैथुनं नैव सेवेत शिरःस्नानञ्च वर्जयेत्।
न प्रीतः परिचक्षीत वहन्न संस्थितोऽपि वा ॥ 27.24 ॥
1.27.m: One should not engage in sexual intercourse, and one should avoid washing one's head; / one should not look at it in delight while carrying [water] or standing [in it].

1.27.s:
medhyāmedhyaśarīratvānnaiva duṣyantyapaḥ kvacit .
vivarṇarasagandhāśca alpāśca parivarjayet .. 27.25 ..
1.27.d:
मेध्यामेध्यशरीरत्वान्नैव दुष्यन्त्यपः क्वचित् ।
विवर्णरसगन्धाश्च अल्पाश्च परिवर्जयेत् ॥ 27.25 ॥
1.27.m: Because water contains both pure and impure bodies, it is never defiled anywhere; / but one should avoid waters that have lost their colour, taste, or smell, or are scanty.

1.27.s:
apāṃ yoniḥ samudraśca tasmāttaṃ kāmayanti tāḥ.
medhyāścaivāmṛtāścaiva bhavanti prāpya sāgaram .. 27.26 ..
1.27.d:
अपां योनिः समुद्रश्च तस्मात्तं कामयन्ति ताः।
मेध्याश्चैवामृताश्चैव भवन्ति प्राप्य सागरम् ॥ 27.26 ॥
1.27.m: The ocean is the source of the waters; therefore they yearn for it. / Reaching the ocean, they become pure and nectar-like.

1.27.s:
tasmādapo na rundhīta samudraṃ kāmayanti tāḥ.
na hinasti bhavo devaḥ sadaivaṃ yo'psu varttate .. 27.27 ..
1.27.d:
तस्मादपो न रुन्धीत समुद्रं कामयन्ति ताः।
न हिनस्ति भवो देवः सदैवं योऽप्सु वर्त्तते ॥ 27.27 ॥
1.27.m: Therefore one should not obstruct the waters; they long for the ocean. / The god Bhava does not harm one who always behaves thus toward water.

1.27.s:
tato'bravīt punarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ kṛṣṇalohitam.
śarvastvamiti yannāma tṛtīyaṃ samudāhṛtam.
tasya bhūmistṛtīyā tu tanurnāmnā bhavatviyam .. 27.28 ..
1.27.d:
ततोऽब्रवीत् पुनर्ब्रह्मा तं देवं कृष्णलोहितम्।
शर्वस्त्वमिति यन्नाम तृतीयं समुदाहृतम्।
तस्य भूमिस्तृतीया तु तनुर्नाम्ना भवत्वियम् ॥ 27.28 ॥
1.27.m: Then Brahmā spoke again to that black-and-red god: / 'As for the name, "You are Śarva," which was uttered as the third, / let this earth be the third body for that [name].'

1.27.s:
ityukte yat sthiraṃ tasya śarīrasyāsthisaṃjñitam.
tadviveśa tato bhūmistasmādbhūḥ śarva ucyate .. 27.29 ..
1.27.d:
इत्युक्ते यत् स्थिरं तस्य शरीरस्यास्थिसंज्ञितम्।
तद्विवेश ततो भूमिस्तस्माद्भूः शर्व उच्यते ॥ 27.29 ॥
1.27.m: When this was said, that which was solid in his body, designated as bone, / into that the earth entered; therefore the earth is called Śarva.

1.27.s:
tasmāt kurvīta no vidvān purīṣammūtrameva vā.
na cchāyāyāṃ na sopāne svacchāyāṃ nāpi mehayet .. 27.30 ..
1.27.d:
तस्मात् कुर्वीत नो विद्वान् पुरीषम्मूत्रमेव वा।
न च्छायायां न सोपाने स्वच्छायां नापि मेहयेत् ॥ 27.30 ॥
1.27.m: Therefore a wise person should not pass feces or urine [thereon], / nor should one urinate in the shade, on steps, or in one's own shadow.

1.27.s:
śiraḥ prāpṛtya kurvīta antarddhāya tṛṇairmahīm.
ya evaṃ varttate bhūmau taṃ śarvo na hinasti vai .. 27.31 ..
1.27.d:
शिरः प्रापृत्य कुर्वीत अन्तर्द्धाय तृणैर्महीम्।
य एवं वर्त्तते भूमौ तं शर्वो न हिनस्ति वै ॥ 27.31 ॥
1.27.m: Covering the head, one should relieve oneself after concealing the earth with blades of grass. / Śarva does not harm one who behaves thus on the earth.

1.27.s:
tato'bravītpunarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ nīlalohitam.
īśāna iti yat‌proktaṃ caturthaṃ nāma te mayā .. 27.32 ..
1.27.d:
ततोऽब्रवीत्पुनर्ब्रह्मा तं देवं नीललोहितम्।
ईशान इति यत्‌प्रोक्तं चतुर्थं नाम ते मया ॥ 27.32 ॥
1.27.m: Then Brahmā spoke again to that blue-and-red god: / 'As for the fourth name, Īśāna, which was spoken to you by me,

1.27.s:
caturthasya caturthī syādvāyurnāmnā tanustava.
ityukte yaccharīrasthaṃ pañcadhā prāṇasaṃjñitam .. 27.33 ..
1.27.d:
चतुर्थस्य चतुर्थी स्याद्वायुर्नाम्ना तनुस्तव।
इत्युक्ते यच्छरीरस्थं पञ्चधा प्राणसंज्ञितम् ॥ 27.33 ॥
1.27.m: the fourth body for the fourth [name] shall be the wind by name.' / When this was said, that which was in the body, fivefold and designated as vital breath,

1.27.s:
viveśa taṃ tadā vāyurīśāno vāyurucyate.
tasmādenaṃ parivadedāyataṃ vāyumīśvaram.
evaṃ yuktamatheśāno naiva devo hinasti tam .. 27.34 ..
1.27.d:
विवेश तं तदा वायुरीशानो वायुरुच्यते।
तस्मादेनं परिवदेदायतं वायुमीश्वरम्।
एवं युक्तमथेशानो नैव देवो हिनस्ति तम् ॥ 27.34 ॥
1.27.m: the wind entered that then; Īśāna is called the wind. / Therefore one should praise this pervasive wind as the Lord; / the god Īśāna does not harm one who is thus devoted.

1.27.s:
tato'bravīt punarbrahmā taṃ devaṃ dhūmralohitam.
yatte paśupatītyuktaṃ mayā nāmeha pañcamam.
pañcamī pañcamasyaiva tanurnāmnā'gnirastu te .. 27.35 ..
1.27.d:
ततोऽब्रवीत् पुनर्ब्रह्मा तं देवं धूम्रलोहितम्।
यत्ते पशुपतीत्युक्तं मया नामेह पञ्चमम्।
पञ्चमी पञ्चमस्यैव तनुर्नाम्नाऽग्निरस्तु ते ॥ 27.35 ॥
1.27.m: Then Brahmā spoke again to that smoky-red god: / 'As for the fifth name, Paśupati, which was spoken by me to you here, / let fire be your fifth body by name for the fifth [name].'

1.27.s:
ityukte yaccharīrasthaṃ tejastasyopasaṃjñitam.
viveśa tattadā hyagnistasmātpaśupatiḥ patiḥ .. 27.36 ..
1.27.d:
इत्युक्ते यच्छरीरस्थं तेजस्तस्योपसंज्ञितम्।
विवेश तत्तदा ह्यग्निस्तस्मात्पशुपतिः पतिः ॥ 27.36 ॥
1.27.m: When this was said, the splendor residing in his body was addressed as such; / then fire indeed entered into that [splendor], therefore Paśupati is the lord.

1.27.s:
candramāstu smṛtaḥ somastasyātmā hyoṣadhīgaṇaḥ.
evaṃ yo varttate vidvān sadā parvaṇi parvaṇi.
na hanti taṃ mahādeva evaṃ vandeta taṃ prabhum .. 27.37 ..
1.27.d:
चन्द्रमास्तु स्मृतः सोमस्तस्यात्मा ह्योषधीगणः।
एवं यो वर्त्तते विद्वान् सदा पर्वणि पर्वणि।
न हन्ति तं महादेव एवं वन्देत तं प्रभुम् ॥ 27.37 ॥
1.27.m: The moon is remembered as Soma, and its self is the host of plants. / The wise man who constantly conducts himself thus at every change of the moon, / Mahādeva does not harm him; thus should he revere that lord.

1.27.s:
gopāyati divādityaḥ prajā naktantu candramāḥ.
ekarātre sameyātāṃ sūryyācandramasāvubhau.
amāvāsyāniśāyāntu tasyāṃ yuktaḥ sadā vaset .. 27.38 ..
1.27.d:
गोपायति दिवादित्यः प्रजा नक्तन्तु चन्द्रमाः।
एकरात्रे समेयातां सूर्य्याचन्द्रमसावुभौ।
अमावास्यानिशायान्तु तस्यां युक्तः सदा वसेत् ॥ 27.38 ॥
1.27.m: The sun protects creatures by day, and the moon by night. / On the single night when both the sun and moon come together— / on the night of the new moon—he should always dwell concentrated on that.

1.27.s:
tatrāviṣṭaṃ sarvamidantanubhirnāmabhiḥ saha.
ekākī yaścaratyeṣaḥ sūryyā'sau candra ucyate .. 27.39 ..
1.27.d:
तत्राविष्टं सर्वमिदन्तनुभिर्नामभिः सह।
एकाकी यश्चरत्येषः सूर्य्याऽसौ चन्द्र उच्यते ॥ 27.39 ॥
1.27.m: All this is pervaded there along with the bodies and the names. / He who wanders alone, that sun is called the moon.

1.27.s:
sūryyasya yat prakāśena vīkṣyante cakṣuṣā prajāḥ.
śuklātmā saṃsthito rudraḥ pibatyambho gabhastibhiḥ .. 27.40 ..
1.27.d:
सूर्य्यस्य यत् प्रकाशेन वीक्ष्यन्ते चक्षुषा प्रजाः।
शुक्लात्मा संस्थितो रुद्रः पिबत्यम्भो गभस्तिभिः ॥ 27.40 ॥
1.27.m: Because of the sun's light, creatures are seen by the eye; / Rudra, abiding white in nature, drinks water with his rays.

1.27.s:
adyate pīyate caivāpyannapānātmakāniyā.
tanurātmabhavā sā vai deheṣvevopacīyate .. 27.41 ..
1.27.d:
अद्यते पीयते चैवाप्यन्नपानात्मकानिया।
तनुरात्मभवा सा वै देहेष्वेवोपचीयते ॥ 27.41 ॥
1.27.m: That which is eaten and drunk, consisting of food and drink, / that body, born of the self, is indeed built up within bodies.

1.27.s:
yayā dhatte prajāḥ sarvāḥ sthirībhūtena cetasā.
pārthivī sā tanustasya śārvī dhārayati prajāḥ .. 27.42 ..
1.27.d:
यया धत्ते प्रजाः सर्वाः स्थिरीभूतेन चेतसा।
पार्थिवी सा तनुस्तस्य शार्वी धारयति प्रजाः ॥ 27.42 ॥
1.27.m: That by which he supports all creatures with a steady mind, / that earthly body of his, Śarva's, sustains creatures.

1.27.s:
yāvat sthitā śarīreṣu bhūtānāṃ prāṇavṛttibhiḥ.
vāyvātmikā tu aiśānī sā prāṇāḥ prāṇinā saha .. 27.43 ..
1.27.d:
यावत् स्थिता शरीरेषु भूतानां प्राणवृत्तिभिः।
वाय्वात्मिका तु ऐशानी सा प्राणाः प्राणिना सह ॥ 27.43 ॥
1.27.m: As long as it remains in the bodies of beings through the functions of the vital breaths, / that [body] consisting of wind is Īśāna's, the breaths along with the breathing creature.

1.27.s:
pītāśitāni pacati bhūtānāṃ jaṭhareṣu yā.
tataḥ pāśupatī tasya pācikā śaktirucyate .. 27.44 ..
1.27.d:
पीताशितानि पचति भूतानां जठरेषु या।
ततः पाशुपती तस्य पाचिका शक्तिरुच्यते ॥ 27.44 ॥
1.27.m: That which cooks what has been drunk and eaten in the bellies of beings, / from that, his cooking power is called Paśupati's.

1.27.s:
yānīha suṣirāṇi syurdeheṣvantargatāni vai.
vāyoḥ sañcaraṇārthāya sā bhīmā cocyate tanuḥ .. 27.45 ..
1.27.d:
यानीह सुषिराणि स्युर्देहेष्वन्तर्गतानि वै।
वायोः सञ्चरणार्थाय सा भीमा चोच्यते तनुः ॥ 27.45 ॥
1.27.m: Whatever hollows there may be internal to bodies / for the circulation of the wind, that is called the terrible body.

1.27.s:
vaitānadīkṣitānāṃ tu yā sthitirbrahmavādinām.
tanurugrātmikā sā tu tenogro dīkṣitaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.46 ..
1.27.d:
वैतानदीक्षितानां तु या स्थितिर्ब्रह्मवादिनाम्।
तनुरुग्रात्मिका सा तु तेनोग्रो दीक्षितः स्मृतः ॥ 27.46 ॥
1.27.m: The condition of the exponents of the Veda initiated into the solemn rites, / that body is of fierce nature; therefore Ugra is remembered as the initiated [sacrificer].

1.27.s:
yattu saṅkalpakaṃ tasya prajāsviha samaṃ sthitam.
sā tanurmmānasī tasya candramāḥ prāṇiṣu sthitaḥ .. 27.47 ..
1.27.d:
यत्तु सङ्कल्पकं तस्य प्रजास्विह समं स्थितम्।
सा तनुर्म्मानसी तस्य चन्द्रमाः प्राणिषु स्थितः ॥ 27.47 ॥
1.27.m: That which is his volitional power abiding equally in creatures here, / that is his mental body, the moon abiding in living beings.

1.27.s:
navo navo bhavati hi jāyamānaḥ punaḥ punaḥ.
nīyate yo yathākāmaṃ vibhudhaiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saha.
mahādevo'mṛtātmā'sau hyammayaścandramāḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.48 ..
1.27.d:
नवो नवो भवति हि जायमानः पुनः पुनः।
नीयते यो यथाकामं विभुधैः पितृभिः सह।
महादेवोऽमृतात्माऽसौ ह्यम्मयश्चन्द्रमाः स्मृतः ॥ 27.48 ॥
1.27.m: He becomes ever new, being born again and again; / he who is led away at will by the gods along with the ancestors, / that Mahādeva, of the nature of nectar and consisting of water, is remembered as the moon.

1.27.s:
tasya yā prathamā nāmnā tanū raudrī prakīrtitā.
patnī suvarcalā tasya putrastasyāḥ śanaiścaraḥ .. 27.49 ..
1.27.d:
तस्य या प्रथमा नाम्ना तनू रौद्री प्रकीर्तिता।
पत्नी सुवर्चला तस्य पुत्रस्तस्याः शनैश्चरः ॥ 27.49 ॥
1.27.m: That body of his which is proclaimed first by the name Raudrī, / Suvarcalā is his wife, and Saturn is her son.

1.27.s:
bhavasya yā dvitīyā tu tanurāpaḥ smṛtā tu vai .
tasyoṣā'tra smṛtā patnī putraścāpyuśanā smṛtaḥ .. 27.50 ..
1.27.d:
भवस्य या द्वितीया तु तनुरापः स्मृता तु वै ।
तस्योषाऽत्र स्मृता पत्नी पुत्रश्चाप्युशना स्मृतः ॥ 27.50 ॥
1.27.m: The second body of Bhava is remembered indeed as the waters; / Uṣā is remembered as his wife here, and Uśanas is remembered as his son.

1.27.s:
śarvasya yā tṛtīyā tu nāma bhūmistanuḥ smṛtā.
patnī tasya vikeśīti putraścāṅgārakaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.51 ..
1.27.d:
शर्वस्य या तृतीया तु नाम भूमिस्तनुः स्मृता।
पत्नी तस्य विकेशीति पुत्रश्चाङ्गारकः स्मृतः ॥ 27.51 ॥
1.27.m: The third body of Śarva is remembered by name as the earth; / Vikeśī is his wife, and Mars is remembered as his son.

1.27.s:
īśānasya caturthasya svargatasya ca yā tanuḥ.
tasya patnī śivā nāma putraścāsya manojavaḥ .. 27.52 ..
1.27.d:
ईशानस्य चतुर्थस्य स्वर्गतस्य च या तनुः।
तस्य पत्नी शिवा नाम पुत्रश्चास्य मनोजवः ॥ 27.52 ॥
1.27.m: And the body of the fourth, Īśāna, who has attained heaven; / his wife is named Śivā, and his son is Manojava.

1.27.s:
nāmnā paśupateryā tu tanuragnirdvijaiḥ smṛtā.
tasya patnī smṛtā svāhā skandaścāpi sutaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.53 ..
1.27.d:
नाम्ना पशुपतेर्या तु तनुरग्निर्द्विजैः स्मृता।
तस्य पत्नी स्मृता स्वाहा स्कन्दश्चापि सुतः स्मृतः ॥ 27.53 ॥
1.27.m: That body of Paśupati which is remembered by the twice-born as fire; / Svāhā is remembered as his wife, and Skanda is remembered as his son.

1.27.s:
nāmnā ṣaṣṭhasya yā bhīmā tanurākāśa ucyate.
diśaḥ patnyaḥ smṛtāstasya svargaścāsya sutaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.54 ..
1.27.d:
नाम्ना षष्ठस्य या भीमा तनुराकाश उच्यते।
दिशः पत्न्यः स्मृतास्तस्य स्वर्गश्चास्य सुतः स्मृतः ॥ 27.54 ॥
1.27.m: The body of the sixth by name Bhīma is called space; / the directions are remembered as his wives, and heaven is remembered as his son.

1.27.s:
ugrā tanuḥ saptamī yā dīkṣitairbrāhmaṇaiḥ smṛtā.
dīkṣā patnī smṛtā tasya santānaḥ putra ucyate .. 27.55 ..
1.27.d:
उग्रा तनुः सप्तमी या दीक्षितैर्ब्राह्मणैः स्मृता।
दीक्षा पत्नी स्मृता तस्य सन्तानः पुत्र उच्यते ॥ 27.55 ॥
1.27.m: The seventh body, Ugrā, which is remembered by initiated brahmins; / Dīkṣā is remembered as his wife, and Santāna is called his son.

1.27.s:
nāmnā'ṣṭamasya mahatastanuryā candramāḥ smṛtaḥ.
patnī tu rohiṇī tasya putraścāsya budhaḥ smṛtaḥ .. 27.56 ..
1.27.d:
नाम्नाऽष्टमस्य महतस्तनुर्या चन्द्रमाः स्मृतः।
पत्नी तु रोहिणी तस्य पुत्रश्चास्य बुधः स्मृतः ॥ 27.56 ॥
1.27.m: The body of the eighth, Mahat, which is remembered by name as the moon; / Rohiṇī is his wife, and Mercury is remembered as his son.

1.27.s:
ityetāstanavastasya nāmabhiḥ parikīrtitāḥ.
tāstu vandya namasyāśca pratināma tanūṣu vai .. 27.57 ..
1.27.d:
इत्येतास्तनवस्तस्य नामभिः परिकीर्तिताः।
तास्तु वन्द्य नमस्याश्च प्रतिनाम तनूषु वै ॥ 27.57 ॥
1.27.m: Thus these bodies of his have been proclaimed along with their names; / they are to be praised and bowed to, body by body according to each name.

1.27.s:
bhakteḥ sūrye'psu pṛthivyāṃ vāyvagnivyomadīkṣite.
tathā ca vai candramasi tanubhirnāmabhiḥ saha.
prajāvāneti sāyujyamīśvarasya naro hi saḥ .. 27.58 ..
1.27.d:
भक्तेः सूर्येऽप्सु पृथिव्यां वाय्वग्निव्योमदीक्षिते।
तथा च वै चन्द्रमसि तनुभिर्नामभिः सह।
प्रजावानेति सायुज्यमीश्वरस्य नरो हि सः ॥ 27.58 ॥
1.27.m: Out of devotion, in the sun, in the waters, in the earth, in the wind, fire, sky, the initiated, / and likewise in the moon, along with the bodies and the names, / that man, possessed of offspring, attains communion with the Lord.

1.27.s:
ityetadvo mayākhyātaṃ guhyaṃ bhīmasya tadyaśaḥ.
śanno'stu dvipade nityaṃ śanno'stu ca catuṣpade .. 27.59 ..
1.27.d:
इत्येतद्वो मयाख्यातं गुह्यं भीमस्य तद्यशः।
शन्नोऽस्तु द्विपदे नित्यं शन्नोऽस्तु च चतुष्पदे ॥ 27.59 ॥
1.27.m: Thus has this secret glory of Bhīma been narrated to you by me. / May there be welfare constantly for our two-footed beings, and may there be welfare for our four-footed beings.

1.27.s:
etat proktaṃ nidānaṃ vastanūnāṃ nāmabhiḥ saha.
mahādevasya devasya bhṛgostu śrṛṇuta prajāḥ .. 27.60 ..
1.27.d:
एतत् प्रोक्तं निदानं वस्तनूनां नामभिः सह।
महादेवस्य देवस्य भृगोस्तु श्रृणुत प्रजाः ॥ 27.60 ॥
1.27.m: This origin of the bodies along with their names has been told to you / for the god Mahādeva; now hear the offspring of Bhṛgu.

1.27.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte mahādevatanuvarṇanaṃ nāma saptaviśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 27 ..
1.27.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते महादेवतनुवर्णनं नाम सप्तविशोऽध्यायः ॥ 27 ॥
1.27.m: Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Bodies of Mahādeva', in the venerable Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.

1.28.s: ..sūta uvāca..
1.28.d: ॥सूत उवाच॥
1.28.m:
The Sūta said:
Then from Bhṛgu was born Khyāti; [and from her] the two lords of pleasure and pain, / the dispensers of good and evil to all living beings here, / the two gods Dhātṛ and Vidhātṛ, who wander through the cosmic ages of Manus.

1.28.s:
bhṛgoḥ khyātirvijajñe'tha īśvarau sukhaduḥkhayoḥ.
śubhāśubhapradātārau sarvaprāṇabhṛtāmiha.
devau dhātāvidhātārau manvantaravicāriṇau .. 28.1 ..
1.28.d:
भृगोः ख्यातिर्विजज्ञेऽथ ईश्वरौ सुखदुःखयोः।
शुभाशुभप्रदातारौ सर्वप्राणभृतामिह।
देवौ धाताविधातारौ मन्वन्तरविचारिणौ ॥ 28.1 ॥

1.28.s:
tayorjyeṣṭhā tu bhaginī devī śrīrlokabhāvinī.
sā tu nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ patimāsādya śobhanam.
nārāyaṇātmajau sādhvī balotsāhau vyajāyata .. 28.2 ..
1.28.d:
तयोर्ज्येष्ठा तु भगिनी देवी श्रीर्लोकभाविनी।
सा तु नारायणं देवं पतिमासाद्य शोभनम्।
नारायणात्मजौ साध्वी बलोत्साहौ व्यजायत ॥ 28.2 ॥
1.28.m: Their elder sister was goddess Śrī, who brings about the welfare of the worlds. / Having obtained the splendid god Nārāyaṇa as her husband, / that virtuous woman gave birth to the two sons of Nārāyaṇa, Bala and Utsāha.

1.28.s:
tasyāstu mānasāḥ putrā ye cānye divyacāriṇaḥ.
ye vahanti vimānāni devānāṃ puṇyakarmaṇām .. 28.3 ..
1.28.d:
तस्यास्तु मानसाः पुत्रा ये चान्ये दिव्यचारिणः।
ये वहन्ति विमानानि देवानां पुण्यकर्मणाम् ॥ 28.3 ॥
1.28.m: Her mind-born sons were those others who move through the sky, / who carry the aerial chariots of the gods of meritorious deeds.

1.28.s:
dve tu kanye smṛte bhāryye vidhāturdhātureva ca.
āyatirniyatiścaiva tayoḥ putrau dṛḍhavratau .. 28.4 ..
1.28.d:
द्वे तु कन्ये स्मृते भार्य्ये विधातुर्धातुरेव च।
आयतिर्नियतिश्चैव तयोः पुत्रौ दृढव्रतौ ॥ 28.4 ॥
1.28.m: Two maidens are remembered as the wives of Vidhātṛ and Dhātṛ: / Āyati and Niyati; and their two sons were firm in their vows:

1.28.s:
pāṇḍuścaiva mṛkaṇḍuśca brahmakośau sanātanau.
manasvinyāṃ mṛkaṇjośca mārkkaṇḍeyo babhūva ha .. 28.5 ..
1.28.d:
पाण्डुश्चैव मृकण्डुश्च ब्रह्मकोशौ सनातनौ।
मनस्विन्यां मृकण्जोश्च मार्क्कण्डेयो बभूव ह ॥ 28.5 ॥
1.28.m: Pāṇḍu and Mṛkaṇḍu, eternal receptacles of the Veda. / And upon Manasvinī, Mārkaṇḍeya was born to Mṛkaṇḍu.

1.28.s:
suto ve daśirāstasya mūrddhanyāyāmajāyata.
pīvaryyāṃ vedaśirasaḥ putrā vaṃśakarāḥ smṛtāḥ.
mārkkaṇḍeyā iti khyātā ṛṣayo vedapāragāḥ .. 28.6 ..
1.28.d:
सुतो वे दशिरास्तस्य मूर्द्धन्यायामजायत।
पीवर्य्यां वेदशिरसः पुत्रा वंशकराः स्मृताः।
मार्क्कण्डेया इति ख्याता ऋषयो वेदपारगाः ॥ 28.6 ॥
1.28.m: His son Vedaśiras was born to Mūrdhanyā. / Upon Pīvarī, sons who continue the lineage were born to Vedaśiras; / they are known as the Mārkaṇḍeyas, seers who have mastered the Veda.

1.28.s:
pāṇḍośca puṇḍarīkāyāṃ dyutimānātmajo'bhavat.
utpannau dyutimantaśca sṛjavānaśca tāvubhau.
tayoḥ putrāśca pautrāśca bhārgavāṇāṃ parasparam.
svāyambhuve'ntare'tīte marīceḥ śrṛṇuta prajāḥ .. 28.7 ..
1.28.d:
पाण्डोश्च पुण्डरीकायां द्युतिमानात्मजोऽभवत्।
उत्पन्नौ द्युतिमन्तश्च सृजवानश्च तावुभौ।
तयोः पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च भार्गवाणां परस्परम्।
स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरेऽतीते मरीचेः श्रृणुत प्रजाः ॥ 28.7 ॥
1.28.m: And from Pāṇḍu upon Puṇḍarīkā, Dyutimān was the son born; / and born were both Dyutimanta and Sṛjavān. / Their sons and grandsons were among the Bhārgavas mutually. / The Svāyambhuva interval having elapsed, hear the offspring of Marīci.

1.28.s:
patnī marīceḥ sambhūtirvijajñe sātmasambhavam.
prajāyate pūrṇamāsaṃ kanyāśvemā vibodhata.
kuṣṭiḥ pṛṣṭistviṣā caiva tathā cāpacitiḥ śubhā .. 28.8 ..
1.28.d:
पत्नी मरीचेः सम्भूतिर्विजज्ञे सात्मसम्भवम्।
प्रजायते पूर्णमासं कन्याश्वेमा विबोधत।
कुष्टिः पृष्टिस्त्विषा चैव तथा चापचितिः शुभा ॥ 28.8 ॥
1.28.m: Sambhūti, the wife of Marīci, gave birth to her own son; / she gave birth to Pūrṇamāsa, and know these daughters: / Kuṣṭi, Pṛṣṭi, Tviṣā, and also auspicious Apaciti.

1.28.s:
pūrṇamāsaḥ sarasvatyāṃ dvau putrāvudapādayat.
virajañcaiva dharmiṣṭhaṃ parvvasañcaiva tāvubhau .. 28.9 ..
1.28.d:
पूर्णमासः सरस्वत्यां द्वौ पुत्रावुदपादयत्।
विरजञ्चैव धर्मिष्ठं पर्व्वसञ्चैव तावुभौ ॥ 28.9 ॥
1.28.m: Pūrṇamāsa fathered two sons upon Sarasvatī: / both Virajas, most righteous, and Parvasa.

1.28.s:
virajasyātmajo vidvān sudhāmā nāma viśrutaḥ.
sudhāmasutavairājaḥ prācyāndiśi samamāśritaḥ .. 28.10 ..
1.28.d:
विरजस्यात्मजो विद्वान् सुधामा नाम विश्रुतः।
सुधामसुतवैराजः प्राच्यान्दिशि सममाश्रितः ॥ 28.10 ॥
1.28.m: The wise son of Virajas was renowned by the name Sudhāman; / Vairāja, the son of Sudhāman, settled equally in the eastern quarter.

1.28.s:
lokapālaḥ sudharmmātmā gaurīputraḥ pratāpavān .
parvasaḥ sarvagaṇānāṃ praviṣṭaḥ sa mahāyaśāḥ .. 28.11 ..
1.28.d:
लोकपालः सुधर्म्मात्मा गौरीपुत्रः प्रतापवान् ।
पर्वसः सर्वगणानां प्रविष्टः स महायशाः ॥ 28.11 ॥
1.28.m: A world-protector, righteous-minded, son of Gaurī, full of valor; / Parvasa, of great renown, entered among all the troops.

1.28.s:
parvasaḥ parvasāyāntu janayāmāsa vai sutau.
yajñavāmañca śrīmantaṃ sutaṃ kāśyapameva ca.
tayorgotrakarau putrau tau jātau dharmaniśvitau .. 28.12 ..
1.28.d:
पर्वसः पर्वसायान्तु जनयामास वै सुतौ।
यज्ञवामञ्च श्रीमन्तं सुतं काश्यपमेव च।
तयोर्गोत्रकरौ पुत्रौ तौ जातौ धर्मनिश्वितौ ॥ 28.12 ॥
1.28.m: Parvasa indeed fathered two sons upon Parvasā: / the glorious Yajñavāma, and the son Kāśyapa; / those two sons who founded family lines were born resolute in righteousness.

1.28.s:
smṛtiścāṅgirasaḥ patnī jajñe tāvātmasambhavau.
putrau kanyāśvatasraśca puṇyāstā lokaviśrutāḥ .. 28.13 ..
1.28.d:
स्मृतिश्चाङ्गिरसः पत्नी जज्ञे तावात्मसम्भवौ।
पुत्रौ कन्याश्वतस्रश्च पुण्यास्ता लोकविश्रुताः ॥ 28.13 ॥
1.28.m: And Smṛti, wife of Aṅgiras, gave birth to her own two / sons and four daughters; they were meritorious and renowned in the world.

1.28.s:
sinīvālī kuhūścaiva rākā cānumatistathā.
tathaiva bharatāgniñca kīrttimantañca tāvubhau .. 28.14 ..
1.28.d:
सिनीवाली कुहूश्चैव राका चानुमतिस्तथा।
तथैव भरताग्निञ्च कीर्त्तिमन्तञ्च तावुभौ ॥ 28.14 ॥
1.28.m:
Sinīvālī, Kuhū, Rākā, and Anumati,
and likewise both Bharata-fire and renowned [Kīrtimant].

1.28.s:
agneḥ putrantu parjanyaṃ saṃhūtī suṣuve prabhum.
hiraṇyaromā parjanyo mārīcyāmudapādayat.
ābhūtasaṃplavasthāyī lokapālaḥ savai smṛtaḥ .. 28.15 ..
1.28.d:
अग्नेः पुत्रन्तु पर्जन्यं संहूती सुषुवे प्रभुम्।
हिरण्यरोमा पर्जन्यो मारीच्यामुदपादयत्।
आभूतसंप्लवस्थायी लोकपालः सवै स्मृतः ॥ 28.15 ॥

1.28.s:
jajñe kīrtimataścāpi dhenukā tāvakalmaṣau.
variṣṭhaṃ dhṛtimantañcāpyubhāvaṅgirasāṃ varau .. 28.16 ..
1.28.d:
जज्ञे कीर्तिमतश्चापि धेनुका तावकल्मषौ।
वरिष्ठं धृतिमन्तञ्चाप्युभावङ्गिरसां वरौ ॥ 28.16 ॥
1.28.m:
And from Kīrtimant, Dhenukā bore those two sinless ones:
Variṣṭha and Dhṛtimant, both best among the descendants of Aṅgiras.

1.28.s:
tayoḥ putrāśca pautrāśca ye'tītā vai sahasraśaḥ.
anasūyāpi jajñe tān pulahasya prajāpateḥ .. 28.17 ..
1.28.d:
तयोः पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च येऽतीता वै सहस्रशः।
अनसूयापि जज्ञे तान् पुलहस्य प्रजापतेः ॥ 28.17 ॥
1.28.m:
Their sons and grandsons, who have passed away in their thousands—
Anasūyā bore them for the Prajāpati Pulaha,

1.28.s:
kanyāñcaiva śrutiṃ nāma mātā śaṅkhapadasya yā.
kardamasya tu yā patnī pulahasya prajāpateḥ .. 28.18 ..
1.28.d:
कन्याञ्चैव श्रुतिं नाम माता शङ्खपदस्य या।
कर्दमस्य तु या पत्नी पुलहस्य प्रजापतेः ॥ 28.18 ॥
1.28.m:
and also a daughter named Śruti, who was the mother of Śaṅkhapada,
and the wife of Kardama, son of the Prajāpati Pulaha.

1.28.s:
satyanetraśca havyaśca āpomūrtiḥ śanīvaraḥ.
somaśca pañcamasteṣāmāsīt svāyambhuve'ntare.
yāme'tīte sahātītāḥ pañcātreyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ .. 28.19 ..
1.28.d:
सत्यनेत्रश्च हव्यश्च आपोमूर्तिः शनीवरः।
सोमश्च पञ्चमस्तेषामासीत् स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे।
यामेऽतीते सहातीताः पञ्चात्रेयाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥ 28.19 ॥
1.28.m:
Satyanetra, Havya, Āpomūrti, Śanīvara,
and Soma was the fifth of them in the cosmic age of Svāyambhuva Manu.
Having passed away together when the Yāma [gods] passed away, they are proclaimed as the five descendants of Atri.

1.28.s:
teṣāṃ putrāśca pautrāśca hyatriṇā vai mahātmanā.
svāyambhuve'ntare yāme śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ .. 28.20 ..
1.28.d:
तेषां पुत्राश्च पौत्राश्च ह्यत्रिणा वै महात्मना।
स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे यामे शतशोऽथ सहस्रशः ॥ 28.20 ॥
1.28.m:
Their sons and grandsons, born indeed of the great-souled Atri
in the cosmic age of Svāyambhuva Manu [during the epoch of] Yāma, numbered in hundreds and thousands.

1.28.s:
prītyāṃ pulastyabhāryāyāṃ dattālistatsūto'bhavat.
pūrvajanmani so'gastyaḥ smṛtaḥ svāyambhuve'ntare.
madhyamo devabāhuśca vinīto nāma te trayaḥ .. 28.21 ..
1.28.d:
प्रीत्यां पुलस्त्यभार्यायां दत्तालिस्तत्सूतोऽभवत्।
पूर्वजन्मनि सोऽगस्त्यः स्मृतः स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे।
मध्यमो देवबाहुश्च विनीतो नाम ते त्रयः ॥ 28.21 ॥

1.28.s:
svasā yavīyasī teṣāṃ sadvatī nāma viśrutā.
parjanyajananī śubhrā patnī tvagneḥ smṛtā śubhā
paulastyasya ṛṣeścāpi prītiputrasya dhīmataḥ.
dattāleḥ suṣuve patnī sujaṅghādīn bahūn sutān.
paulastyā iti vikhyātāḥ smṛtāḥ svāyambhuve'ntare .. 28.23 ..
1.28.d:
स्वसा यवीयसी तेषां सद्वती नाम विश्रुता।
पर्जन्यजननी शुभ्रा पत्नी त्वग्नेः स्मृता शुभा
पौलस्त्यस्य ऋषेश्चापि प्रीतिपुत्रस्य धीमतः।
दत्तालेः सुषुवे पत्नी सुजङ्घादीन् बहून् सुतान्।
पौलस्त्या इति विख्याताः स्मृताः स्वायम्भुवेऽन्तरे ॥ 28.23 ॥
1.28.m:
Their younger sister was celebrated by the name Sadvatī,
the radiant mother of Parjanya, remembered as the auspicious wife of Agni.
And the wife of the wise Dattāli, son of Prīti and seer born of Pulastya,
bore many sons, Sujaṅgha and others.
They are renowned as the descendants of Pulastya, remembered in the cosmic age of Svāyambhuva Manu.

1.28.s:
kṣamā tu suṣuve putrān pulahasya prajāpateḥ.
te nāgnivarcasaḥ sarve yeṣāṃ kīrtiḥ pratiṣṭhitā .. 28.24 ..
1.28.d:
क्षमा तु सुषुवे पुत्रान् पुलहस्य प्रजापतेः।
ते नाग्निवर्चसः सर्वे येषां कीर्तिः प्रतिष्ठिता ॥ 28.24 ॥
1.28.m:
Kṣamā bore sons to the Prajāpati Pulaha;
they all possessed the splendour of fire, and their fame was established:

1.28.s:
kardamaścāmbarīṣaśca sahiṣṇuśceti te trayaḥ .
ṛṣirdhanakapīvāṃśca śubhā kanyā ca pīvarī .. 28.25 ..
1.28.d:
कर्दमश्चाम्बरीषश्च सहिष्णुश्चेति ते त्रयः ।
ऋषिर्धनकपीवांश्च शुभा कन्या च पीवरी ॥ 28.25 ॥
1.28.m:
Kardama, Ambarīṣa, and Sahiṣṇu were the three,
and the seer Dhanakapīvat, and the auspicious maiden Pīvarī.

1.28.s:
kardamasya śrutiḥ patnī ātreyya janayatsutān.
putraṃ śaṅkhapadañcaiva kanyāṃ kāmyāṃ tathaiva ca .. 28.26 ..
1.28.d:
कर्दमस्य श्रुतिः पत्नी आत्रेय्य जनयत्सुतान्।
पुत्रं शङ्खपदञ्चैव कन्यां काम्यां तथैव च ॥ 28.26 ॥
1.28.m:
Kardama's wife Śruti, born of Atri, bore children:
a son, Śaṅkhapada, and likewise a daughter, Kāmyā.

1.28.s:
sa vai śahkhapadaḥ śrīmān lokapālaḥ prajāpatiḥ.
dakṣiṇasyāṃ diśi rataḥ sāmyāṃ dattvā priyavrate .. 28.27 ..
1.28.d:
स वै शह्खपदः श्रीमान् लोकपालः प्रजापतिः।
दक्षिणस्यां दिशि रतः साम्यां दत्त्वा प्रियव्रते ॥ 28.27 ॥
1.28.m:
That glorious Śaṅkhapada was a guardian of the world and a Prajāpati;
devoted to the southern quarter, having bestowed equal status upon Priyavrata.

1.28.s:
kāmyā priyavratāllebhe svāyambhuvasamān sutān.
daśakanyādvayañcaiva yaiḥ kṣatraṃ sampravartitam .. 28.28 ..
1.28.d:
काम्या प्रियव्रताल्लेभे स्वायम्भुवसमान् सुतान्।
दशकन्याद्वयञ्चैव यैः क्षत्रं सम्प्रवर्तितम् ॥ 28.28 ॥
1.28.m:
From Priyavrata, Kāmyā obtained sons equal to Svāyambhuva [Manu],
and ten pairs of daughters by whom the ruling class was propagated.

1.28.s:
putro dhanakapīvāṃśca sahiṣṇurnāma viśrutaḥ.
yaśodhārī vijajñe vai kāmadevaḥ sumadhyamaḥ .. 28.29 ..
1.28.d:
पुत्रो धनकपीवांश्च सहिष्णुर्नाम विश्रुतः।
यशोधारी विजज्ञे वै कामदेवः सुमध्यमः ॥ 28.29 ॥
1.28.m:
The son Dhanakapīvat was celebrated by the name Sahiṣṇu;
Yaśodharā gave birth to Kāmadeva of slender waist.

1.28.s:
ṛtoḥ kratusamaḥ putro vijajñe santatiḥ śubhā.
naiṣāṃ bhāryasti putro vā sarve te hyūrddhva retasaḥ.
ṣaṣṭyetāni sahasrāṇi vālakhilyā iti śrutāḥ .. 28.30 ..
1.28.d:
ऋतोः क्रतुसमः पुत्रो विजज्ञे सन्ततिः शुभा।
नैषां भार्यस्ति पुत्रो वा सर्वे ते ह्यूर्द्ध्व रेतसः।
षष्ट्येतानि सहस्राणि वालखिल्या इति श्रुताः ॥ 28.30 ॥

1.28.s:
aruṇasyāgrato yānti parivārya divākaram.
ābhūtasaṃplavātsarve pataṅgasahacāriṇaḥ .. 28.31 ..
1.28.d:
अरुणस्याग्रतो यान्ति परिवार्य दिवाकरम्।
आभूतसंप्लवात्सर्वे पतङ्गसहचारिणः ॥ 28.31 ॥
1.28.m:
Surrounding the sun, they go in front of Aruṇa;
all of them accompany the sun until the dissolution of all beings.

1.28.s:
svasārau tu yavīyasyau puṇyātmasumatī ca te.
parvasasya snuṣe te vai pūrṇamāsasutasya vai .. 28.32 ..
1.28.d:
स्वसारौ तु यवीयस्यौ पुण्यात्मसुमती च ते।
पर्वसस्य स्नुषे ते वै पूर्णमाससुतस्य वै ॥ 28.32 ॥
1.28.m:
The two younger sisters, virtuous-minded and pure-souled,
were indeed the daughters-in-law of Parvasa, the son of Pūrṇamāsa.

1.28.s:
ūrjāyāntu vasiṣṭhasya putrā vai sapta jajñire.
jyāyasī ca svasā teṣāṃ puṇḍarīkā sumadhyamā .. 28.33 ..
1.28.d:
ऊर्जायान्तु वसिष्ठस्य पुत्रा वै सप्त जज्ञिरे।
ज्यायसी च स्वसा तेषां पुण्डरीका सुमध्यमा ॥ 28.33 ॥
1.28.m:
Upon Ūrjā, seven sons were born to Vasiṣṭha,
and their elder sister was the slender-waisted Puṇḍarīkā,

1.28.s:
jananī sā dyutimataḥ pāṇḍostu mahiṣī priyā .
asyāṃ tvime yavīyāṃso vāsiṣṭhāḥ sapta viśrutāḥ .. 28.34 ..
1.28.d:
जननी सा द्युतिमतः पाण्डोस्तु महिषी प्रिया ।
अस्यां त्विमे यवीयांसो वासिष्ठाः सप्त विश्रुताः ॥ 28.34 ॥
1.28.m:
the mother of Dyutimant and beloved queen of Pāṇḍu.
And in her were born these seven renowned younger descendants of Vasiṣṭha:

1.28.s:
rajaḥ putro'rddhabāhuśca savanaścādhanaśca yaḥ.
sutapāḥ śukla ityete sarve saptarṣayaḥ smṛtāḥ .. 28.35 ..
1.28.d:
रजः पुत्रोऽर्द्धबाहुश्च सवनश्चाधनश्च यः।
सुतपाः शुक्ल इत्येते सर्वे सप्तर्षयः स्मृताः ॥ 28.35 ॥
1.28.m:
Rajaḥputra, Ardhabāhu, Savana, Anadhana,
Sutapas, and Śukla—all these are remembered as the seven seers.

1.28.s:
rajaso vāpyajanayanmārkaṇḍeyī yaśasvinī.
pratīcyāṃ diśi rājanyaṃ ketumantaṃ prajāpatim .. 28.36 ..
1.28.d:
रजसो वाप्यजनयन्मार्कण्डेयी यशस्विनी।
प्रतीच्यां दिशि राजन्यं केतुमन्तं प्रजापतिम् ॥ 28.36 ॥
1.28.m:
The renowned Mārkaṇḍeyī also bore to Rajas
in the western quarter the royal Ketumant, a Prajāpati.

1.28.s:
gotrāṇi nāmabhisteṣāṃ vāsiṣṭhānāṃ mahātmanām.
svāyambhuventare'tītāstvagnestu śrṛṇuta prajāḥ .. 28.37 ..
1.28.d:
गोत्राणि नामभिस्तेषां वासिष्ठानां महात्मनाम्।
स्वायम्भुवेन्तरेऽतीतास्त्वग्नेस्तु श्रृणुत प्रजाः ॥ 28.37 ॥
1.28.m:
The lineages of those great-souled descendants of Vasiṣṭha bear their names.
They passed away in the cosmic age of Svāyambhuva Manu; now hear of the progeny of Agni.

1.28.s:
ityeṣa ṛṣisargastu sānubandhaḥ prakīrttitaḥ.
vistareṇānupūrvyā cāpyagnestu śrṛṇuta prajāḥ .. 28.38 ..
1.28.d:
इत्येष ऋषिसर्गस्तु सानुबन्धः प्रकीर्त्तितः।
विस्तरेणानुपूर्व्या चाप्यग्नेस्तु श्रृणुत प्रजाः ॥ 28.38 ॥
1.28.m:
Thus this creation of the seers together with its succession has been proclaimed
in detail and in due order; now hear of the progeny of Agni.

1.28.s: iti śrīmahāpurāṇe vāyuprokte ṛṣivaṃśānukīrttanaṃ nāmāṣṭāviṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 28 ..
1.28.d: इति श्रीमहापुराणे वायुप्रोक्ते ऋषिवंशानुकीर्त्तनं नामाष्टाविंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 28 ॥
1.28.m: Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, entitled 'The Recitation of the Lineage of the Seers', in the glorious Mahāpurāṇa spoken by Vāyu.
